# Omni View Top World News
> **Ukraine says seven drones sank a Russian warship off Libya, 1,500 miles from the front.**

**What You Need to Know:** Ukraine says seven naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury off Libya and hit a cargo ship, a claim Moscow has not confirmed and that eastern Libyan authorities treat as an attack on their port. Oxfam says contamination now covers more than 99 percent of Gaza, and the U.S. Justice Department admitted in court that it deported a citizen. This edition also draws on the Omni View Omni View North America desk.

### The Ten
**Ukraine sinks Russian warship off Libya in latest expansion of the war: NBC News**
Ukraine's president said Monday that Ukrainian forces sank a Russian warship in the Libyan port of Benghazi on Sunday and struck a cargo ship, in an operation Ukraine's Security Service put about 1,500 miles from the established front. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said seven Ukrainian-made naval drones sank the corvette Merkury, which he described as one of Russia's newest ships, commissioned in 2023, and hit the transport ship Angara, calling it an exemplary Ukrainian operation. NBC News reported that he posted footage of drones approaching vessels and of fireballs. The Security Service said the corvette regularly escorted naval convoys and guarded the Angara, which it said carried weapons, that both were legitimate military targets, and that the drones were launched from a mother ship after delivery to a set point. It said a Ka-27 helicopter on the corvette was also sunk, despite attempts to destroy the drones from the air. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow had noted Zelenskyy's statement and left comment to the defence ministry, which had not yet spoken; Al Jazeera reported no official Russian comment and that it was unclear whether anyone was killed. Libya's eastern administration said an explosion struck a Russian vessel docked at Benghazi Naval Base on its way back to Russia after a stop to refuel, and called a strike inside a Libyan port a serious assault on sovereignty, without naming Ukraine. Saddam Haftar, deputy commander of the eastern forces, said Libya rejects the use of its territory to settle scores, while the United Nations Support Mission in Libya demanded an immediate, independent and transparent investigation. The eastern health ministry said every crew member from the cargo ship had been rescued and was being treated; Libya has been split since 2011 between a U.N.-backed government in Tripoli and a rival eastern administration tied to Russia.
Ranks: crews and port workers in Benghazi, plus Ukraine and Russia at war · a claimed sinking far outside the Black Sea, disputed by silence from Moscow · already done Sunday, with an investigation called now Source: [nbcnews.com](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/ukraine/ukraine-sinks-russian-warship-merkury-libya-naval-drones-war-rcna610822)
Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/23/zelenskyy-says-ukraine-behind-drone-attacks-on-russian-ships-near-libya)

**‘Environmental crimes’: Israel blamed for toxic pollution in 99% of Gaza: Al Jazeera**
In the Gaza Strip, Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory say Israel's explosives and incendiary weapons have contaminated more than 99 percent of the territory, which they call a toxic wasteland for about 2.3 million people. Amitabh Behar, Oxfam's international executive director, said assaults on Gaza's environment are environmental war crimes that threaten life now and for generations, and that Palestinians are exposed through air, food, water, soil and rubble. The groups used satellite imagery, remote sensing, scientific analysis and open-source data, and they point to the highest concentrations in Gaza City, Jabalia and North Gaza. Al Jazeera, citing the report, said the war has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians, and that more than 1,500 have been killed since a ceasefire signed in October 2025. A U.N. commission of inquiry said in September 2025 that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza; the International Court of Justice is hearing a genocide case and said in January that it was plausible Israel had committed genocide. The U.N. Environment Programme estimates 61 million tonnes of debris, about 29 tonnes for each person living in Gaza now, and Oxfam says clearing it would take 2.1 million dump-truck loads. By 11 October 2025, Oxfam estimates, Israeli ground operations had directly affected about 283 square kilometres of Gaza's 365, or 78 percent, and more than 90 percent of Palestinians had been forcibly displaced. A study cited in the report put direct conflict emissions above 1.3 million tonnes of carbon-dioxide equivalent by January 2025. Oxfam said a full independent investigation is urgently needed to identify and reduce the risks.
Ranks: about 2.3 million people in Gaza · contamination reported across 99 percent of the land they live on · already in soil, water and air, with effects the authors say will last generations Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/23/environmental-crimes-israel-blamed-for-toxic-pollution-in-99-of-gaza)
Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/11/23/gaza-turned-into-toxic-wasteland-by-israels-war-says-new-report?traffic_source=rss)

**Trump administration deported US citizen to Mexico, DoJ admits in court: The Guardian**
In the United States, the Justice Department admitted in federal court on Friday that it had deported a U.S. citizen to Mexico after authorities wrongly concluded he was undocumented. Brian José Morales García, 25, of Austin, Texas, was born in Denver and raised in Mexico; he was a passenger in a work vehicle stopped near Fredericksburg on 3 April, without identification, and he told officers his birth certificate and Social Security card were at home. Customs and Border Protection agent Robert Gil Jr consulted Mexican records that listed a Mexican birthplace, accused him of saying he was born in Mexico, and noted that he spoke only Spanish, according to court records cited by The Guardian. He was deported on 7 April, and the administration later said in a media statement that he had been in the country illegally. His lawyers sued on 1 May, saying he had falsely admitted an illegal entry and signed rapid-deportation papers because agents threatened imprisonment, and that family and friends were turned away when they tried to deliver proof of citizenship. On Friday the department denied that account, said he went to Mexico voluntarily and therefore had no basis to sue, and still conceded he was allowed back on 30 August after a review of his place of birth. U.S. Attorney Justin Simmons wrote that Morales García is a dual citizen of the United States and Mexico. Judge Robert Lee Pitman did not immediately rule on the request to dismiss; an October 2025 ProPublica report found agents had detained more than 170 U.S. citizens in the first nine months of President Donald Trump's second term, and Texas's public safety department works with federal immigration authorities under the 287(g) program.
Ranks: one citizen already deported, and others in similar stops · loss of home and work for months, then a court fight still open · back in the U.S. since 30 August; the dismissal request is undecided Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/23/trump-administration-deported-citizen-mexico)

**The worst COP ever? Climate talks collapse in chaos: France 24**
In Turkey, COP31's final agreement was rejected on Sunday, ending the talks in failure. France 24 said a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels. The summit ran two days past its schedule. The network called that stretch record overtime and the ending chaotic. It said the collapse underscored strains on diplomacy in a fractured world. On Monday, several Pacific island nations expressed despair and disappointment that the U.N. talks had produced no final agreement on the climate crisis. France 24 said those small states are among the places most exposed to seas rising because of human-caused warming.
Ranks: governments at the Turkey summit, and Pacific island populations · no agreed climate text after a scheduled close · already failed Sunday; island governments answered Monday Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261123-the-worst-cop-ever-climate-talks-collapse-in-chaos)
Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/environment/20261123-let-down-on-all-sides-pacific-island-nations-express-despair-over-cop31-failure)

**Rule changes leave international students rethinking plans to study in the U.S.: The Globe and Mail**
In the United States, first-time international students at colleges and universities fell 15 percent this fall after a 17 percent drop the year before, according to the Institute of International Education. Applications by Canadians to first-year U.S. undergraduate programs for fall 2027 fell 13 percent from the previous year, according to Common App. In March 2025, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the United States had revoked more than 300 student visas and was looking to revoke more every day; by January 2026 the State Department said it had revoked some 8,000, including for protests and social-media activity. Some students were told their records on the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System had been terminated, which blocks class registration and practical training; others were arrested and detained. In April 2025, government lawyers told courts that Immigration and Customs Enforcement would restore those records but keep the power to terminate them again. The State Department told The Globe and Mail the United States remains the world's leading destination for international students. Zuzana Cepla Wootson of the Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration, a plaintiff in one lawsuit that helped reverse some terminations and a group working with almost 600 campuses, said an atmosphere of fear remains because the rules keep changing. An unnamed Ontario lawyer who studied at Georgetown said he erased his social-media accounts, and a British Columbia science student said classmates at Northwestern University use a private app called Fizz to warn one another about immigration raids nearby.
Ranks: international students on U.S. campuses, and Canadians applying for 2027 · a 15 percent drop in new enrolments and thousands of visa revocations · already in this year's intake, with applications still falling Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-rule-changes-international-students-rethinking-study-us/)

**German police respond to multiple school bomb threats: DW**
German police are checking school bomb threats they do not treat as credible, and Denmark is reporting a similar series of apparent hoaxes.
Ranks: pupils and parents in several German cities, and in Denmark · schools disrupted while police treat the warnings as not credible · happening Monday Source: [dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/german-police-respond-to-multiple-school-bomb-threats/a-80018842?maca=en-rss-en-world-4025-rdf)

**Chamonix mayor plans tourist limits for Alpine beauty spot: The Guardian**
Chamonix's mayor plans tourist limits after as many as 4,000 people a day visit Lac Blanc, more than double the 2020 numbers.
Ranks: summer visitors to Lac Blanc and wildlife on those trails · crowding, litter and damage the mayor says already spoil the lakes · a limit is planned, not yet in force Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/chamonix-mayor-tourist-limits-lac-blanc)

**Daily cannabis use more common among Canadian adults than daily alcohol consumption, study finds: The Globe and Mail**
In Canada, a medical-journal study of nearly 100,000 adults finds daily cannabis use is now more common than daily drinking.
Ranks: Canadian adults in a national health survey · daily cannabis ahead of daily alcohol, including among people under 35 · measured in 2023–2024 and published Monday Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-daily-cannabis-use-more-common-among-canadian-adults-than-daily/)

**'Out of control': ICE arrests at Seattle airport spark outcry: France 24**
Washington's governor called federal agents out of control after officers detained a father and daughter on a Seattle airport jet bridge.
Ranks: the father and daughter detained Saturday, and passengers who filmed it · an arrest in a boarding bridge by masked officers in unmarked jackets · already done; the governor answered in public Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261123-out-of-control-ice-arrests-at-seattle-airport-spark-outcry)

**Dozens Unaccounted for After Fire Rips Through Candy Factory in Indonesia: The New York Times**
Dozens remain unaccounted for after a fire tore through an Indonesian candy factory where hundreds were present on Saturday.
Ranks: hundreds who were in the factory compound · dozens still unaccounted for after a blaze that lasted hours · the fire began Saturday; the search is the current fact Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/23/world/asia/indonesia-factory-fire.html)

### Both Sides: Should Natural England be abolished?
Britain's first secretary of state, Louise Haigh, has put every arm's-length body in view for devolution, dissolution, or a return into a department, and she has not ruled out abolishing Natural England. The case reported for scrapping the nature watchdog is that faster planning could boost housebuilding and growth. Last month the Conservatives said that if they won power they would abolish Natural England and the Environment Agency to help create more homes. Haigh's own reason is institutional. She told Sky News that successive governments created more quangos, pushed decisions out of departments, and then objected when those bodies decided differently, and that her government is committed to devolving responsibilities where they can be devolved. On BBC Radio 4 she said all such bodies are in her sight to be devolved to mayors and strategic authorities, brought back under a secretary of state, or dissolved entirely. She did not say Natural England will be abolished. Tony Juniper, the chair of Natural England, answered the reports by saying he is proud of work to unite national ambitions for growth with nature's recovery, and that healthy nature is not opposed to economic development but enables it. The Guardian said removing or curbing the watchdog would be likely to prompt concern from environmental groups. Haigh spoke Monday before a CBI speech in which she argued for greater public control of water and energy, sectors where she said privatisation had not worked, a separate argument from the quango review. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/23/natural-england-could-be-abolished-quango-cull-louise-haigh)

# Omni View Top World News
> **Two people were injured, Bahrain says, in an Iranian strike on an industrial site.**

**What You Need to Know:** Two people were injured, Bahrain says, in an Iranian strike that set a civilian industrial site on fire, even as Bahrain’s Interior Ministry separately reported material damage and no injuries. A new U.S. study says Washington can renew the Iran fight but not readily deter China, while cost-of-living marches continued from Portugal to France. This edition also draws on the Omni View Omni View North America desk.

### The Ten
**Bahrain says Iranian attack caused fire at industrial facility: Al Jazeera**
Bahrain said an Iranian attack on a civilian industrial facility caused a fire, and The National reported that Bahrain said two people were injured. The Bahraini Defence Force said defences intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks late on Saturday, after sirens sounded, the ministry told residents to move to the nearest safe place, and an all-clear followed. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps said the operation answered continued violations of Iranian airspace, including by U.S. MQ-1 and MQ-9 drones, and an attack on a radar installation on Hengam Island. The IRGC said missile and drone strikes targeted U.S. military positions at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases, that two radars belonging to U.S. Army Patriot air defence systems were struck, and that any further airspace violation would meet a harsh and decisive response. Bahrain hosts the U.S. Navy’s Fifth Fleet and has been attacked repeatedly since the U.S.-Israel war on Iran began in late February, including three drone attacks in recent days after a lull of several weeks; Al Jazeera reported that other Gulf states have also come under repeated fire from Tehran since that war began. The Bahrain attack came as multiple tankers were reportedly struck in the Strait of Hormuz, through which about one-fifth of the world’s oil passed before the war; U.S. Central Command said last month it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer, while the IRGC claimed U.S. escort and aerial protection had failed and caused significant losses to equipment and vessels under U.S. protection. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said a Qatari delegation visited Tehran the previous evening and held two hours of talks, and state television quoted Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying ongoing regional talks must be given a chance and the blockade must be lifted rationally. Iran’s demands, as reported, include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the U.S. counterblockade of Iranian ports, and Araghchi’s reported line is that discussion of opening the Strait of Hormuz is pointless until those demands are met. Bahrain’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called on the U.N. Security Council to take firm measures to compel Iran to implement Resolution 2817.
Ranks: Gulf civilians, U.S. forces in Bahrain, and oil shippers · a fire, disputed injuries, and claimed radar strikes · immediate Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/21/bahrain-says-iranian-attack-causes-fire-at-industrial-facility) Source: [thenationalnews.com](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/mena/2026/11/22/live-bahrain-attack-iran-war/)

**The U.S. has sufficient munitions to fight Iran — but what about China?: Deseret News**
The United States has sufficient munitions to renew the fight with Iran, according to an analysis the Center for Strategic and International Studies released this month, but the same analysis says there is great concern about a war with China. Rebuilding inventories, CSIS said, will require a multiyear commitment extending beyond the current crisis, and the report calls for a long-term national commitment to aggressive munitions production. Some inventories are in good shape, others are not, and a few are critically short; of high concern are costly ballistic missile defence systems, Patriot and THAAD, used heavily in the opening stages of the Iran war. Ballistic missile defence interceptors are in critical short supply, CSIS noted, and even before the Iran war such weaponry was already considered inadequate for a war against China, with no battlefield substitutes once supplies are diminished. Only highly specialized munitions can intercept theater ballistic missiles that reach a velocity of 5,000-plus mph in their terminal phase, the report noted, while aircraft and cruise missiles fly at about 800 mph and drones at 150-250 mph. An estimated two-thirds of the country’s prewar Patriot interceptor inventory have reportedly been expended defending against Iranian ballistic missiles, and Lockheed Martin has a goal to produce 2,000 Patriot interceptors each year, up from around 600. About half of the prewar THAAD inventory is estimated to have been expended in the Iran war, according to the CSIS analysis; Standard Missiles have not been used as widely, partly because they launch from naval vessels and U.S. ships have been stationed outside the Persian Gulf. A large supply of air-to-air missiles remains in U.S. inventory. Last summer on CBS News’ “Face the Nation,” Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth labeled claims of a munitions stockpile shortage a “manufactured story” and said supplies “are only getting stronger,” while Senator Mark Kelly, Democrat of Arizona, said it is widely understood that attacking 10,000 targets from the air uses a lot of munitions and “we do not have an endless supply of these things.” It is unclear if or when President Donald Trump will order resumption of major military actions against Iran.
Ranks: U.S. forces and anyone relying on deterrence of China · interceptor stocks cut by an estimated half to two-thirds · multiyear Source: [deseret.com](https://www.deseret.com/u-s-world/2026/11/22/munitions-military-iran-china-trump/)

**Europe sees new protests over rising costs, inequality and public services: France 24**
France saw the sixth consecutive weekend of marches over the cost of living, public services and inequality, as Sunday marked a third consecutive day of protests across Europe, from Portugal to France, after large demonstrations on Friday and smaller rallies on Saturday. France 24 reported that the protests have largely focused on the rising cost of living and access to affordable housing. The movement, sparked in mid-September by high school students calling for improved learning conditions, has since fuelled a nationwide campaign against soaring prices, failing public services and police brutality, Al Jazeera reported. Across France, organisers reported 150,000 protesters on Saturday, down from 200,000 last week and 800,000 during the first of the weekly demonstrations on October 17. The Ministry of the Interior said numbers have “significantly declined,” putting Saturday’s turnout at 82,500 people, compared with 106,000 a week earlier. The protests have been largely peaceful but have seen sporadic violence on the margins and repeated accusations of police brutality. Last month, huge rallies across France descended into the worst rioting seen in years, with hundreds of shops looted and buildings attacked and set on fire. Unions and activists have called for further protests in the coming weeks.
Ranks: marchers from Portugal to France, organisers citing 150,000 in France · pressure on prices, housing and services, with turnout down since October · this weekend and coming weeks Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe-sees-new-protests-over-rising-costs-inequality-and-public-services) Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/gallery/2026/11/22/photos-people-rally-across-france-over-living-costs-public-services?traffic_source=rss)

**South Korea education minister resigns over exam cheating scandal: BBC**
South Korea’s education minister, Choi Kyo-jin, resigned on Sunday over an exam-cheating scandal, and President Lee Jae Myung, who has been calling for an overhaul of the exam system, accepted the resignation. Choi said he took full responsibility for confusion caused by last-minute measures aimed at stopping AI-assisted cheating during Thursday’s college entrance exam, known as the Suneung, telling Yonhap he could not escape criticism that the ministry failed to prepare in advance. The Suneung takes up to nine hours and plays a big role in the career trajectories of millions of South Koreans; about 500,000 students sat it this year. The education ministry said 111 candidates were found with unauthorised smart devices. A week earlier, Han Won-seok, 34, the top scorer in April’s national tax accountancy exam, with one wrong answer out of 160, admitted using a microcamera, a mobile phone and AI. In a video message he said he photographed the questions, sent them to an AI, and checked answers on his smartphone. Authorities then sent three nationwide emergency alerts between 08:00 and 15:00 local time on Thursday, the first use of the national disaster alert system to catch exam cheaters; phones blared even on silent, including tourists on data roaming, but not if switched off or on airplane mode. Candidates had to cover buttons on shirts and jackets, and authorities inspected eyewear. France 24 reported that the controversy centred on that tax-exam admission of a miniature camera and smartphone.
Ranks: about 500,000 Suneung candidates and the education ministry · a minister out, 111 devices found, and a new alert tactic · already in effect Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw3dgk29d37no?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss) Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/south-korea-ai-cheating-sparks-exam-security-chaos)

**Ontario Liberals choose Navdeep Bains as new leader: The Globe and Mail**
Canada’s Ontario Liberals chose Navdeep Bains as leader on Saturday, the third leader since 2020 elected without a seat in the provincial legislature. Bains, a former industry minister in Justin Trudeau’s government, won on the third ballot with 50.3 per cent, to 49.7 per cent for Toronto MPP Lee Fairclough, before about 1,000 Liberals at the Metro Toronto Convention Centre. The party is trying to rebuild after three consecutive election losses and present an alternative to Premier Doug Ford’s Progressive Conservatives. Bains told reporters he will seek a seat and will not ask one of the current 14 MPPs to resign; he was elected five times federally in Mississauga and Brampton and left his post as chief corporate affairs officer at Rogers Communications earlier this spring. Fairclough, a first-term MPP for Etobicoke-Lakeshore, is a former hospital executive and national women’s rugby player; Stephanie Bowman finished third and Dylan Marando fourth. In his victory speech Bains said people have fallen behind economically and cannot find a family doctor, and that Ford and the Conservatives “have abandoned the fight” and “are in it for their buddies.” He cited the previous Liberal government’s creation of full-day kindergarten, reduced class sizes, and the Greenbelt, an environmentally protected area of more than 800,000 hectares around Greater Toronto; the RCMP has for three years been investigating the Ford government’s decision to open that region to development, a move since reversed, and Ford has consistently denied wrongdoing. Bains also said the party will “reverse OSAP, ASAP,” after the government scaled back the Ontario Student Assistance Program and now faces questions about alleged abuse by private career colleges. The Globe and Mail reported he is the first racialized person to lead any major party in the province; the Progressive Conservatives criticized his ties to Trudeau, who formally resigned as federal Liberal leader in March 2025, with Citizenship and Multiculturalism Minister Graham McGregor among those speaking.
Ranks: Ontario Liberal members and the province’s opposition · a new leader by less than one point, still without a seat · from Saturday Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-ontario-liberal-party-new-leader-navdeep-bains/)

**Incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries Vows to End Iran War, Levy Sanctions on Violent Settlers: Haaretz**
U.S. speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries wants a settler-violence bill within a hundred days, besides an early end to the Iran war.
Ranks: the next U.S. House and people in the Iran war and the West Bank · a pledge, not yet a vote · January Source: [haaretz.com](https://www.haaretz.com/us-news/2026-11-22/ty-article/hakeem-jeffries-vows-to-end-iran-war-levy-sanctions-on-violent-settlers/000001a2-027d-d175-abf6-1e7d38a80000) Source: [middleeastmonitor.com](https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20261122-hakeem-jeffries-vows-early-push-to-end-iran-war-calls-gaza-devastation-unacceptable/)

**Who Is the Mexican Drug Kingpin Known as El Chapo Isidro?: The New York Times**
Mexico captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, El Chapo Isidro, one of the F.B.I.’s ten most wanted fugitives, in a violent operation.
Ranks: Mexican security forces and trafficking networks tied to a most-wanted fugitive · a capture · already done Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/21/world/americas/mexico-el-chapo-isidro-drug-kingpin.html)

**Deadly Protests Erupt in Bangladesh Over Exiled Former Leader. What to Know.: The New York Times**
Deadly protests erupted in Bangladesh as supporters of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina, sentenced to death in absentia, waged a small-scale insurgency.
Ranks: Bangladesh’s government and Hasina’s supporters · street protests and a described insurgency · underway Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/21/world/asia/bangladesh-protests-sheikh-hasina-what-to-know.html)

**China, ASEAN countries struggle over South China Sea code of conduct: DW**
The Philippines wanted a South China Sea code of conduct by 2026, but disagreements with China are slowing an ASEAN deal.
Ranks: coastal states and ships in the South China Sea · no code by the Philippines’ 2026 aim · ongoing Source: [dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/china-asean-countries-struggle-over-south-china-sea-code-of-conduct/a-80009799?maca=en-rss-en-world-4025-rdf)

**Indian opposition party’s youth wing warns of more Meta protests after police clashes: The Guardian**
India’s Congress youth wing warned of further protests after police clashes Friday outside Meta’s Hyderabad offices over removed accounts.
Ranks: Congress youth members and Meta’s India offices · more protests warned after Friday clashes · timing unstated Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/india-congress-meta-protests-police-hyderabad)

### Both Sides: Where Colorado conservatives put their money
What is being argued now, after the votes are in, is where Colorado’s conservative donors should spend next: more ballot measures, or the Republican Party’s own candidates and infrastructure. Advance Colorado and its allies spent millions to place six measures before voters, on taxes, energy, criminal justice and elections. Michael Fields, the group’s president, and former state GOP chair Dick Wadhams say the losses follow the scale of the Democratic wave. Wadhams’s best reason is the record he cites: nobody wins everything, and Advance has been an important counterweight to Democratic control of the state. Fields adds that the measures were identified broadly as a conservative slate, which made them an easier target in a blue environment. Frank McNulty, a University of Colorado regent and the last Republican speaker of the Colorado House, says that playbook has come to an end. His best reason is tactical: throwing fifteen ballot initiatives at the wall, not funding the campaigns behind them, and hoping they pass does not work anymore. Colorado GOP chair Craig Steiner tells donors that ballot fights must be repurchased every two years, while a larger presence in the statehouse could do some of the same work in law. The election is the shared ground. All but one Advance measure was trailing on election night. The one that passed, Proposition 132, increases criminal penalties for possessing or distributing fentanyl, and Steiner notes Democrats’ minority-proof legislature can amend it. Two measures the group opposed passed, setting aside billions for schools and healthcare and raising income taxes on the highest earners, which The Denver Post says upends decades of revenue restrictions conservatives had defended. Steiner said he will make the case that the party and the candidates are the better cost-benefit.

# Omni View Top World News
> **Two Russian missiles and a drone fell in Poland, testing NATO's line on collective defence.**

**What You Need to Know:** Two Russian missiles and a drone fell on Polish territory during Russia's overnight attack on Ukraine, and Warsaw is treating the hits as a deliberate test of the alliance. Poland's defence minister says the weapons came down in the southeast on November 20, with no immediate injuries, while the prime minister calls it an intentional provocation. This edition also draws on the Omni View Omni View North America desk.

### The Ten
**Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?: Al Jazeera**

In Poland, a NATO member on Ukraine's western border, the government says Russian weapons fell on its territory during the night of November 20, while Russia was bombarding Ukraine and European troops were drilling in the southeast. Poland's Defence Minister, Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, told a news conference in Warsaw that two missiles and a jet-powered drone came down in the country's southeast. He placed the missiles at Nowy Lipowiec and Rudnik nad Sanem, and the drone at Molodycz. Al Jazeera reports that security cameras captured the moment a suspected Russian missile struck Polish territory during that attack on Ukraine. The government says Poland may have been hit by two missiles and a jet-powered drone. No immediate injuries or damage were reported.

The geography is what turns debris into a political fact. One missile is believed to have crashed about 35 kilometres, or 22 miles, from where European troops were exercising. A Kh-101 cruise missile went down about 50 kilometres, or 31 miles, from the Ukrainian border. What officials believe was a jet-powered drone hit about 30 kilometres, or 20 miles, from that border. The incidents came as the United States pushes to revive talks on ending the war in Ukraine, and they have raised the question of whether the strike was deliberate. Al Jazeera's account notes that Warsaw accuses Moscow of intentional provocation, while the bar for triggering NATO's collective-defence clause remains high.

That same night, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia fired more than 400 drones and at least 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, some with cluster warheads. He said at least eight civilians were killed and more than two dozen were wounded. Al Jazeera describes the barrage as one of Russia's heaviest bombardments of Ukraine. The Polish impacts are therefore not a separate skirmish in the reporting. They are objects that left the attack on Ukraine and came down inside a treaty ally, close to a border and close to foreign troops who were already in the field.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk said it appeared "we are dealing with an intentional provocation" by Russia. He said the incident was likely timed to coincide with the European military exercises in Poland. Those exercises are described as unprecedented. The two-week drill began on November 9 in southeastern Poland. It is preparing forces for a possible post-war mission in Ukraine, to help stabilise the country and rebuild its military. Eleven countries are holding the exercises. One impact is believed to have landed about 35 kilometres from that training ground, so the drill and the debris share the same southeastern corner of the country.

Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at the Clinton Institute, University College Dublin, told Al Jazeera the incident "fits into a pattern going back for months" of Russia "testing how far they can go." He said that a few months ago the pattern was drones flown into airspace, and that a couple of times fighter jets were flown across the border into the Baltic states. "You just test how NATO responds," he said. This time, he said, Moscow had "gone a bit further." "You lob a couple of missiles across and a drone" near where 11 countries are holding exercises. His reading is a sequence, not a finding of intent by a court: drones, then jets, then missiles and a drone beside a multinational drill.

The Polish Air Force had already launched preventive air patrols on September 17, aimed at securing the eastern part of Polish airspace after repeated incursions in the previous weeks. That date sits two months before the November 20 impacts and three weeks before the November 9 start of the southeastern exercise. The week of the hits therefore has a longer runway in the same reporting: patrols in September, a two-week drill from November 9 aimed at a possible post-war mission, an American push to revive talks, and then weapons on the ground on November 20.

Harry Nedelcu, partner and senior director for geopolitics at Rasmussen Global, told Al Jazeera the testing has not been limited to Poland. "During the war, there's been repeated instances of Russia testing NATO allies – Poland, Romania and also non-NATO Moldova as well, which is experiencing – especially over the last few months – increasing numbers of drones and missiles flying over its territory and airspace," he said. He tied the incursions to a core Russian war aim: preventing Ukraine from being part of NATO. He said the full-scale invasion has lasted almost five years, and that Moscow's goal is to undermine the alliance. "What Russia is doing with these missiles, drones, that sometimes find their way into NATO territory, tests NATO just under the radar of Article 5 to see how far can they push things. How far can they take hybrid warfare?" he said. Article 5 is the collective-defence clause. Al Jazeera's framing is that the bar for triggering it remains high even as Warsaw accuses Moscow of intentional provocation.

What changes, and for whom, follows from those distances and from that framing. People in three southeastern Polish localities — Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem, and Molodycz — now have a recorded impact, even with no immediate injuries or damage reported. The troops of 11 countries, already in a drill that began on November 9 and pointed at a possible post-war mission in Ukraine, were within about 35 kilometres of one impact. Ukrainians absorbed, on Zelenskyy's numbers, a night of more than 400 drones and at least 110 missiles, among them 27 ballistic missiles, some with cluster warheads, with at least eight civilians killed and more than two dozen wounded. NATO governments are left with a Polish prime minister calling the episode an intentional provocation, a defence minister naming two missiles and a drone, and analysts describing a months-long test kept, in Nedelcu's words, just under Article 5. The United States, in the same reporting, is pushing to revive talks on ending the war. A strike that Polish leaders call deliberate, landing while those talks are being pushed and while European forces rehearse a mission inside Ukraine, is the decision point the day actually contains: not a declared alliance war, and not a confirmed Russian admission in this account, but a named allied government's account of weapons on its soil and an open question, which Al Jazeera puts in the headline, of whether NATO responds.

The distinction the reporting keeps is between a claim and a finding. Kosiniak-Kamysz stated the impacts as fact at a Warsaw news conference: two missiles, one jet-powered drone, three named places, the night of November 20. Tusk's sentence is a judgement of purpose: an intentional provocation, likely timed to the exercises. Lucas and Nedelcu supply the pattern they say the night fits — months of drones and jets, tests of Poland, Romania, and Moldova, a war aim of keeping Ukraine out of NATO. Cameras, Al Jazeera says, captured a suspected Russian missile striking Polish territory. Officials believe one object was a Kh-101 and another a jet-powered drone. Those labels are official belief and ministerial statement, not a published forensic report in the articles. No immediate injuries or damage were reported, which is why the consequence is political and military rather than a casualty count inside Poland. The people it changes something for, and soon, are the residents of those three places, the Ukrainian civilians under that night's barrage, the soldiers of 11 countries whose drill sat about 35 kilometres from one impact, and the governments that must decide whether a high bar for Article 5 still holds after a prime minister has called the night deliberate.

Ranks: People in southeastern Poland, Ukrainian civilians under that night's barrage, and the troops of 11 exercising countries · a NATO member records impacts and calls them provocation, with no immediate Polish injuries reported · immediate, response unstated Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/21/russian-missiles-hit-poland-what-happened-and-could-nato-respond) Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/21/russian-missiles-hit-poland-what-happened-and-could-nato-respond?traffic_source=rss)

### Both Sides: Should the EU cut Russian travel after Denmark's allegation?
Denmark is asking European Union governments to answer a plot it says Russian intelligence planned and started, and that Danish security services say they stopped. The person named by Danish media is the rapper Kyivstoner, whose real name is Albert Vasiliev, a Ukrainian-American. Denmark's security and intelligence agency, PET, said it stopped individuals who were intending to kill him at a concert in September. Three individuals were stopped in a car near the venue on 25 September. Firearms and knives were found in the vehicle. Two people have been charged with attempted murder and with assisting a foreign intelligence service, and both pleaded not guilty. PET said the individuals were associated with a banned Danish gang, Loyal to Familia, which the agency describes as known for extensive, serious and violent criminal activity. PET worked with police on the case. Denmark's foreign minister said Russia's defence attaché will now be expelled and must leave within seven days.

The case for tighter travel rules is Denmark's, joined by the European Commission president. Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen called the alleged attempt Russian intimidation meant to make Denmark waver in its support for Ukraine. In a message to EU governments, confirmed by two diplomats and seen by Reuters, Denmark urged "concrete actions" demonstrating European strength against Moscow, including further restrictions on Russian nationals' access to the Schengen zone, a halt to tourist visas for Russian citizens, and a Schengen-wide policy of not recognising Russian non-biometric passports. Rasmussen said Copenhagen was already very reluctant to issue visas, but Russians can still obtain a Schengen visa in another country and travel to Denmark. He wants such visas to apply only in the issuing country. Denmark would present the proposals to EU ambassadors in Brussels on Monday. France 24 reports that Danish authorities have ordered the expulsion of a Russian diplomat and announced tighter restrictions on visas for Russian tourists. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Saturday she strongly condemns an assassination attempt against a US-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark, orchestrated, she said, by Russian intelligence services. "This was an attack on EU soil. And it is unacceptable," she said, adding that the EU stands in full solidarity with Denmark and with all member states targeted by Russian hybrid attacks. She said Russia's hybrid threats are becoming less and less hybrid, and more and more real, and that the EU will soon propose a new European Security Strategy to reinforce preparedness and deterrence.

The case against is the Russian embassy's in Copenhagen, and Moscow's stated intention to answer the expulsion. The embassy said on Friday the accusations were not backed with proof. It called the allegations unsubstantiated and said Copenhagen failed to provide evidence of Moscow's involvement. It described a "Danish model" in which a "Russian trace" is discovered and "exploited for a propaganda spectacle," and accused Denmark of provocations meant to frighten the Danish population and justify a prolonged confrontation with Russia. Russian state media cite the foreign ministry in Moscow as saying it will respond to the expulsion of its official "accordingly." Separately, Russia's FSB security service accused Vasiliev and the Ukrainian authorities in July of organising a "terrorist attack" on military facilities and personnel in Russia. The rapper denied that allegation on social media. The two people charged pleaded not guilty. Those pleas are not findings. What happens next is dated: Denmark takes the visa and passport proposals to EU ambassadors on Monday, the defence attaché has seven days to leave, and von der Leyen says a new European Security Strategy will be proposed soon.

### Progress Watch
Ukrainian forces have liberated 14 settlements and reclaimed nearly 200 square kilometres, about 77 square miles, in the Kharkiv region in a counteroffensive codenamed Bear Trap, according to BBC News Ukraine on November 20, as reported by UNITED24 Media. The operation disrupted a Russian offensive, codenamed Bear Corner, that began in late June 2026 and aimed at encircling Ukrainian troops near Prykolotne and capturing about 500 square kilometres. BBC News Ukraine said Russian troops had established positions near Vilkhuvatka and threatened Ukrainian supply routes, and that Ukrainian commanders deployed additional forces to the sector in September. The counteroffensive began on September 20. Rather than hitting Russian positions head-on, Ukrainian troops used armoured assaults to draw reinforcements toward Vilkhuvatka, then struck the concentrated forces with 18 Fire Point fixed-wing attack drones, advanced from two flanks, and by October 10 had reportedly completed the encirclement. The 475th Separate Assault Regiment CODE 9.2 was a key assault unit, with the multidomain centre Phalanx coordinating planning. CODE 9.2 released footage of M1 Abrams and T-80 tanks, Bradley infantry fighting vehicles, attack drones, and assault teams near Vilkhuvatka. Its figures of about 911 Russian personnel losses and nearly 400 pieces of equipment damaged or destroyed have not been independently verified. Ukrainian forces also used drones to mine Russian logistics routes up to 30 kilometres deep, on a mesh network that worked without Starlink, and used StarGate heavy-lift drones for seven evacuations of wounded soldiers over several weeks. Lieutenant Colonel Oleksandr Nastenko, callsign Flint, commander of CODE 9.2, told BBC News Ukraine the operation remains ongoing, with troops still clearing settlements near the Russian border. The Ukrainian military says the counteroffensive has stabilised the sector, despite Russian Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov reporting to Vladimir Putin on October 16 that Moscow's encirclement operation had been completed. In October, Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps completed Operation Vivaldi in the Donetsk region, reporting the recapture of 16 settlements and 277 square kilometres. Source: [united24media.com](https://united24media.com/war-in-ukraine/ukraine-springs-bear-trap-on-russian-forces-liberating-14-villages-and-200-sq-km-24587)

# Omni View Top World News
> **Almost one hundred Russian missiles hit three Kyiv bridges, killing people and closing the capital's routes.**

**What You Need to Know:** Almost one hundred Russian missiles hit three Kyiv bridges, killing people and closing the capital's routes. The United States, China and Russia then issued a symbolic peace declaration in Shenzhen, while Britain and the European Union moved toward easier food trade and youth travel. This edition also draws on the Omni View Omni View North America desk.

### The Ten
**Three Kyiv bridges hit during major Russian missile attack: BBC World**
In Ukraine, Russia hit three bridges in Kyiv overnight, the BBC reports, in a nationwide assault that also struck railway stations days after Ukraine damaged the Crimean Bridge. President Volodymyr Zelensky called it one of the most massive strikes of the war and said it left at least eight dead; the BBC reported five people killed. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched almost 100 missiles and around 400 drones, and air force spokesman Yuriy Ignat called the attack one of the most powerful yet. The Podilsko-Voskresensky, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges were closed, and Mayor Vitali Klitschko urged people to avoid driving into the city unless necessary, saying a critical facility was damaged and seven medical personnel were injured. Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky said 28 people were injured across nine regions, including an ambulance hospital in Kharkiv. In Lviv, Mayor Andriy Sadovyi said two people were killed at the Sknyliv railway station and ten were injured, with rescue work still going on. Polish Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said a Russian cruise missile landed about 50 kilometres, or 31 miles, from Poland's border with Ukraine, and that two further projectiles fell in nearby villages and harmed no one; Polish and Swedish jets scrambled and were later stood down. President Vladimir Putin had said retaliation for the Crimean Bridge strike would be far more painful, after Zelensky said Ukraine's operation had been weeks in the making. The barrage began hours after UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said they were ready for talks with Moscow, as the Kremlin pushed back on a US claim that Russia could accept Western-backed security guarantees for Ukraine. US envoy Jared Kushner said the United States wants to make a deal with Europe by his side.
Ranks: people in Kyiv, nine Ukrainian regions, and villages in southeast Poland · bridges shut, deaths and injuries, a missile on NATO territory · overnight, and still this morning Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6x29gn4pdn9o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

**Trump, Xi and Putin release ‘peace declaration’ from unprecedented summit: Hawaii Tribune-Herald**
In China, the United States, China and Russia agreed a symbolic peace declaration on Thursday at a three-way summit in Shenzhen, the Hawaii Tribune-Herald reports, and reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The leaders pledged United Nations reforms, larger supplies of fuel products for all countries, and the immunity of state officials in international courts, and said they would discuss cutting nuclear risks, with no date set. President Vladimir Putin said the declaration set no ambitious goals and that nobody would be forced to comply with it. Trump greeted Putin as his friend, was hugged by President Xi Jinping, told NBC the meeting rated a 12 on a scale of zero to 10, and told Reuters the summit was bigger than Yalta. He said it is better to have people with 4,000 nuclear weapons as a friend than as an enemy, and that giving those weapons up is not easy. Foreign Minister Wang Yi said the three would keep coordinating at working level, and Trump said he would hold a news conference in Washington at noon today. The Reuters account said the three-day Asia trip yielded few tangible victories despite Trump's claims of making history.
Ranks: governments and publics tied to US, Chinese and Russian nuclear and oil policy · a symbolic text, not a binding arms deal or a Ukraine settlement · already issued; Trump's Washington briefing is set for noon today Source: [hawaiitribune-herald.com](https://www.hawaiitribune-herald.com/2026/11/20/nation-world-news/trump-xi-and-putin-release-peace-declaration-from-unprecedented-summit/)

**U.K. and EU hold rare summit as Burnham seeks to mend Brexit damage: The Globe and Mail**
In Belgium, Prime Minister Andy Burnham met European Council President António Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in Brussels on Friday for only the second UK-EU summit since Britain left the bloc, The Globe and Mail reports. The package on the table would let up to 100,000 young adults from each side live and work in the other for up to three years, link emissions trading, and drop checks on food and farm goods. Burnham said the deals could add 0.5 percent to Britain's economy, up from an earlier 0.4 percent, and he cited Treasury analysis putting the gain at up to 0.5 percent, calling it the largest growth step of this Parliament. An EU official, speaking on condition of not being named, said nothing takes effect unless the two sides agree university tuition fees within six months; EU negotiators want European students in Britain to pay domestic rather than foreign fees, which the UK has resisted. EU sources told The Guardian that tying the food deal to fees is meant to offset leverage London would gain from a six-month delay on tuition while Britain seeks a place in Made in Europe rules aimed at supply chains and China. France has insisted the UK cannot have a vote on food and drink legislation, and talks continue on access to those manufacturing rules. The deals require Britain to accept some EU standards it does not help write, and Burnham has said rejoining is one option, not a near one, and would need British voters plus every EU government's support. Von der Leyen said she wanted more chances for young people, easier agrifood trade and closer economic-security cooperation; Burnham pitched the package as a way to cut supermarket prices.
Ranks: shoppers, exporters and young adults in Britain and the EU, on the order of 100,000 each way · cheaper food trade and temporary work rights, if a fee deal follows · Friday's summit now; fee talks over the next six months Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-uk-eu-summit-burnham-brexit/) Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/20/uk-eu-european-union-brexit-deal-andy-burnham-latest-news-updates)

**Liberals’ 2026 budget passes in House of Commons: Global News**
In Canada, the House of Commons passed the 2026 federal budget by 162 votes to 151, Global News reports, after it was tabled on November 5. The plan sets out billions of dollars in new borrowing and tax measures aimed mainly at infrastructure and other capital projects, including a $36-billion productivity deduction meant to push firms to buy machinery. Liberals now hold a majority after byelections and floor-crossings, unlike last year, when Green leader Elizabeth May cast the deciding vote and two New Democrat and two Conservative MPs abstained or were absent. Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre has argued the borrowing hands costs to Canadians and does not make life more affordable. Parliamentary budget officer Annette Ryan warned about the scale of borrowing but found the government narrowly on track to keep its fiscal anchors, with higher oil prices and stronger revenues improving the books since spring. Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne said confident countries invest, and that Canada is one of the few G7 countries able to fund growth and affordability measures at the same time. New Democrat Leader Avi Lewis said his MPs would vote against a plan he argues serves big business rather than groceries, phones, housing and health care, and Bloc Québécois Leader Yves-François Blanchet criticized the title Maîtres Chez Nous as failing to give Quebec more control of its affairs. Implementation bills can still be amended in committee, and the second implementation act for the 2025 budget, tabled in May, is still before Parliament.
Ranks: taxpayers, firms and lower-income households across Canada · billions in new borrowing, a capital push, and benefit top-ups, still short of final law · the House vote is done; implementation bills follow Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12158925/budget-2026-passes/)

**Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin announces presidential bid: France 24**
In France, former prime minister Dominique de Villepin said on Friday he will run for president in 2027, France 24 reports, joining an already crowded field. He announced the bid at Paris's Maison de l'Amérique Latine and, through his team, set himself against three forces he said are cutting the country apart: the National Rally, France Unbowed, and the Macronist centre, which he accused of France's decay. He asked voters not to accept what he called a death foretold, and offered himself as renewal. His party is Humanist France; he has published a book, expanded his social media presence and spoken around the country after more than two years of preparing a run. His team says he has pledges from 300 mayors toward the 500 signatures needed to get on the ballot, the same hurdle that kept him off it in 2012. He was a chief strategist for Jacques Chirac from the 1980s and foreign minister during France's opposition to the US-led invasion of Iraq in 2003, and he has never been elected to public office. His opposition to Israel's campaign in Gaza has drawn attention from younger and more left-leaning voters who once would have dismissed a conservative former premier.
Ranks: French voters weighing the 2027 field · another declared candidate, still short of the signatures required to stand · the announcement is today; the election is in 2027 Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261120-former-french-prime-minister-dominique-de-villepin-to-announce-presidential-bid)

### Both Sides: Should Britain accept EU rules to reset post-Brexit trade?
Britain is deciding whether a reset with the European Union should bind it to standards it does not write, and to a later bargain on what EU students pay to study in the UK, before easier food trade and youth movement can take effect. Prime Minister Andy Burnham makes the case for going ahead. He says the Brexit Britain was given has not worked, and that the country lost more than it gained. A closer partnership, he argues, is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe, because it cuts costs and opens chances for the young. He told businesses in Brussels the two sides were pretty much there and that it was a really good deal, and he has put every future option on the table, including a return to the bloc, while stressing that reversal is only one possible outcome and is not close. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage makes the case against. He told the BBC he is afraid the great Brexit debate has just started again, and that it very soon becomes a choice of whether Britain rejoins or stays out. Supporters of Brexit say taking rules London does not set undermines the independence the leave vote was meant to secure. European sources describe a hard bargain rather than a gift: tying food access to a fee settlement is meant to blunt leverage Britain would otherwise hold, and France has insisted the UK get no vote on food and drink law. What happens next is negotiation, not a finished treaty. The coming months are when the fee fight, and the argument over who writes the rules, either settle or stall the reset.

### Progress Watch

Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/20/pill-pancreatic-cancer-breakthrough-daraxonrasib)

# Omni View Top World News
> **10,000 Rohingya were killed, the world court says, in the first ruling that a state committed genocide.**

**What You Need to Know:** The International Court of Justice has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the first time that court has found a state responsible for the crime, and Al Jazeera reports the court's president said evidence shows forces killed some 10,000 Rohingya. The same day, U.S., Chinese and Russian leaders closed a first three-way meeting by agreeing a nuclear war must never be fought, and Israeli forces finished a rare push beyond Gaza's Yellow Line. This edition also draws on the Omni View Omni View North America desk.

### The Ten
**Myanmar committed acts of genocide against Rohingya minority, world’s top court rules: The Guardian**
Myanmar was found by the International Court of Justice in The Hague, on Thursday, to have committed acts of genocide against the Rohingya during military “clearance operations” in 2016 and 2017, and The Guardian reports the court has never previously found a state responsible for genocide. Court president Yuji Iwasawa said the court was fully convinced that Myanmar committed acts under the Genocide Convention with intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population in Myanmar. Al Jazeera reports Iwasawa said evidence shows Myanmar’s forces killed some 10,000 Rohingya, and that security forces killed thousands of civilians, perpetrated widespread sexual violence and extreme violence against children, and attacked people as they fled toward Bangladesh. The Guardian reports the 2016–17 campaign forced more than 700,000 mostly Muslim Rohingya into Bangladesh; Al Jazeera puts that flight at more than 730,000, and says more than 1.3 million Rohingya remain displaced, including 1.2 million in camps in Cox’s Bazar. The Guardian says more than 1 million still live in those Bangladesh camps and that fewer than 600,000 are estimated to remain in Myanmar. The Gambia filed the case in 2019 for survivors, resting on genocidal statements and patterns of conduct in Rakhine state, including shooting people as they fled and blocking their return. Myanmar denied a genocide and said it was answering attacks by the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army; the court said the only reasonable inference from the atrocities was intent to destroy a substantial part of the group, and that Myanmar violated its obligation to prevent genocide. The Guardian reports the court cannot enforce its rulings, though they are considered binding and can shape sanctions, and that governments watched in part because the judgment is a precedent for other genocide claims, including a case against Israel. Min Aung Hlaing, who headed the military during the attacks, has a pending International Criminal Court arrest warrant on allegations of crimes against humanity; he overthrew Aung San Suu Kyi’s elected government in a 2021 coup and was installed as civilian president in April after elections The Guardian describes as widely discredited.
Ranks: Rohingya survivors and more than a million refugees · a binding genocide finding, with enforcement still diplomatic · the judgment is in now Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/19/genocide-rohingya-international-court-of-justice-ruling-myanmar) Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/19/un-top-court-finds-myanmar-killed-10000-rohingya-as-it-rules-on-genocide?traffic_source=rss)

**Trump, Xi and Putin sit down for a rare three-way meeting in China: CBS News**
In China, Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin agreed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, ending their first trilateral talks after about an hour and a half on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. A Kremlin readout said the three exchanged views on the international situation, reaffirmed strategic stability and international security, and, as permanent members of the Security Council, recommitted to reforming the United Nations so it can meet global challenges. That readout said they committed to increasing oil and gas production for the benefit of all countries, stressed state consent and respect for the immunities of state officials, and said the International Criminal Court and similar bodies should not abuse their powers. Trump opened by saying, “We are really making history,” and that no peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement. Putin said the three had numerous shared interests in settling regional conflicts, including the conflict in Ukraine. Xi did not refer to Ukraine directly; he said that when major powers live in harmony the world is at peace and when they clash the world falls into turmoil, and Xinhua, cited by Al-Monitor, quoted him saying nuclear weapons should be prohibited and eliminated toward a world free of them.
Ranks: the three nuclear powers and countries touched by the Ukraine and Iran wars · a shared pledge, not a new disarmament treaty · the statement is out, no next date named Source: [cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-xi-putin-china-apec-summit/) Source: [al-monitor.com](https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/11/trump-xi-putin-conclude-historic-meeting-ukraine-war-nuclear-arms)

**Israeli military completes ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line: BBC**
In Gaza, Israeli forces completed a ground operation east of Nuseirat refugee camp and onto the main north-south road, west of the Yellow Line that the Israeli military says marks more than 60 percent of the territory Israel occupies. The Israel Defense Forces said the operation, with the Shin Bet, was aimed at dismantling a “terror tunnel” that posed an immediate and direct threat to its troops, and the BBC reports it was the first incursion beyond that line the military had publicly announced since the October 2025 ceasefire. Hamas, which controls the rest of Gaza, said the advance of military vehicles and the evacuation of residents were a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire. Gaza’s Hamas-run government media office said an estimated 6,000 people fled homes and tents and called that the war crime of forced displacement. Gaza’s Hamas-run Civil Defence agency said three people were killed and others wounded in three Israeli drone strikes on Wednesday, in Nuseirat, Gaza City and Deir al-Balah; the IDF told the BBC it had struck several military operatives. A Nuseirat resident told BBC Arabic of indiscriminate fire and numerous casualties, including fatalities; asked about those reports, the IDF sent a general statement about the operation. Cogat warned people north of Nuseirat and Bureij to stay away and closed a section of Salah al-Din road, then said Thursday morning the activity had ended and the road had reopened. The BBC reports near-daily Israeli strikes have continued for 13 months, and that conditions for the 2.1 million people in Gaza remain dire.
Ranks: people near Nuseirat and Gaza’s 2.1 million residents · a finished one-day push, with displacement and deaths disputed · the military says the operation is over Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw8r7510degno?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

**Tusk appears to mock Trump’s Putin comment as Ukraine’s allies meet in Berlin: The Guardian**
In Germany, the leaders of Germany, France, Britain, Poland and Italy met in Berlin on Thursday with NATO secretary general Mark Rutte, France 24 reports, as a show of support for Kyiv while Trump and Putin were in China. U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were also attending, and France 24 says the gathering has fed European fears that decisions on the war could be made without Europe. Poland’s prime minister Donald Tusk, one of Europe’s five negotiators, wrote on X, “God, protect us from such friends,” which The Guardian reports was an apparent reference to Trump’s greeting of Putin. Foreign minister Radosław Sikorski told reporters it was difficult to judge, and that by their fruits they shall know them. Sikorski said the optics of hugging Putin and calling him a friend caused concern, and asked whether Trump was more a friend to Putin or to Poland’s president, and which friend he would choose if push came to shove.
Ranks: Ukraine and the European governments at the Berlin table · a public show of support and alarm, no new decision named · the meeting is today Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/19/russia-ukraine-war-coalition-of-the-willing-europe-latest-news-updates) Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/ukraine-s-european-allies-meet-in-berlin-in-show-of-support)

**AI lab Anthropic sets stock market record with $81 billion IPO: France 24**
In the United States, Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, is going public as what France 24 calls the first pure-play AI lab to list, in a debut the BBC describes as a stock-market record that will make it one of the most valuable firms in the world. The BBC reports Anthropic is raising 81 billion dollars. NPR reports the company is raising more than 100 billion dollars. France 24 puts the valuation at 1.5 trillion dollars. France 24 calls the listing a bellwether amid growing concerns of a financial bubble in the sector. The same France 24 report says a scientific study shows U.S. data centres are emitting as much greenhouse gas as entire nations. The two raise figures are each outlet’s number, not a single confirmed sum.
Ranks: Anthropic’s prospective shareholders and the AI industry · a record listing, with the raise disputed between outlets · the debut is this week’s news, trading date unstated Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/business/20261119-ai-lab-anthropic-sets-stock-market-record-with-81-billion-ipo) Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6742m39xgzxo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss) Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/19/nx-s1-6042558/anthropic-ipo-breaks-records-100-billion)

**South Korea's top court overturns charges against ex-prime minister for his role in martial law: CBC**
South Korea’s Supreme Court overturned former prime minister Han Duck-soo’s conviction for aiding the December 2024 martial-law declaration.
Ranks: Han Duck-soo and South Korea’s martial-law cases · a conviction set aside · the ruling is in Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/south-korea-overturns-charges-against-ex-prime-minister-9.7427717?cmp=rss)

**In Bending to Trump, Law Firm Did $11.8 Million of Free Work for Administration: The New York Times**
In the United States, The New York Times reports a law firm did 11.8 million dollars of free work for the Trump administration.
Ranks: the administration and that firm’s clients · 11.8 million dollars of free legal work · already performed Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/19/us/politics/kirkland-ellis-law-firm-trump.html)

**How the War in Iran Will Remake the Global Energy Order: The New York Times**
The International Energy Agency found the Iran war’s oil shock could accelerate alternative power, The New York Times reports.

**FIFA confirms Diallo, Tashima as Infantino’s challengers at 2027 election: Al Jazeera**
FIFA confirmed France’s Philippe Diallo and Japan’s Kozo Tashima as the only other candidates for its 2027 presidency.
Ranks: FIFA’s member associations · the 2027 field is now set · the vote is next year Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11/19/fifa-confirms-diallo-tashima-as-infantinos-challengers-at-2027-election?traffic_source=rss)

**Ukrainian NGO head says Russian attacks on infrastructure are a sign of desperation: The Globe and Mail**
In Ukraine, a nongovernmental leader told The Globe and Mail that Moscow, stuck on the battlefield, is hitting civilian targets.
Ranks: Ukrainian civilians under infrastructure attack · a claim of desperation, not a new casualty count · the attacks are described as ongoing Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-ukrainian-ngo-head-says-russian-attacks-on-infrastructure-are-a-sign/)

### Both Sides: Israel’s push west of Gaza’s Yellow Line
The question is whether Israel’s ground push west of the Yellow Line in central Gaza was a limited answer to an immediate threat or a breach of the October 2025 ceasefire. The Israel Defense Forces say the operation was targeted, run with the Shin Bet, and aimed at a “terror tunnel” west of the line that posed an immediate and direct threat to Israeli troops. On that account, the advance removed a danger to forces along a line the military says marks more than 60 percent of Gaza under Israeli control, and Cogat told Palestinians on Thursday morning that the activity had ended and that Salah al-Din road had reopened. Hamas, which controls the rest of Gaza, says the advance of Israeli military vehicles beyond the Yellow Line and the evacuation of residents were a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement. Gaza’s Hamas-run government media office says an estimated 6,000 people fled homes and tents and that the flight was the war crime of forced displacement. The casualty accounts do not match: the Hamas-run Civil Defence agency said three people were killed in drone strikes on Wednesday, a Nuseirat resident told the BBC of numerous casualties including fatalities, and the IDF said it had struck several military operatives and answered the casualty reports with a general statement about the operation. Cogat has told residents the push is over; Hamas’s statement treats the crossing of the line itself as the breach. Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw8r7510degno?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)
