# Omni View Top World News
> **Half a day without Outlook has left businesses and governments unable to work.**

**What You Need to Know:** Half a day without Outlook has left businesses and governments unable to work, as a Microsoft email failure entered a second day. Oil supply is set to exceed demand for the first time since the Iran war, and President Donald Trump said Washington does not need a deal with Tehran. This edition also draws on the Omni View Omni View North America desk.

### The Ten
**Microsoft outages extend into 2nd day, company not aware of malicious activity: CBC**
A failure in Microsoft services tied to Exchange Online and email is in a second day. CBC reported Friday that an hourslong outage was affecting a wide range of Microsoft 365 offerings that interact with those email services. Users reported Outlook, Teams and the Copilot assistant down. France 24 reported that the break began on Thursday and was still hitting people around the world on Friday, November 13. Microsoft blamed server problems and said it was struggling to fix them. The company said malicious activity was not to blame, and that it was not aware of malicious activity. It also reported making headway on the repair. France 24 said businesses, governments and likely millions of people have been without services like Outlook email for over half a day, triggering wide-ranging consequences. France 24’s tech correspondent Peter O’Brien said the scale and duration make it one of the biggest outages ever. Offices and public agencies that run mail and meetings on those tools are the ones living through the second day.
Ranks: businesses, governments and likely millions of users · email and collaboration tools down for over half a day · immediate, into a second day Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/microsoft-outage-friday-activity-9.7420313?cmp=rss)
Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261113-microsoft-faces-a-major-outlook-outage-no-signs-of-a-cyberattack)
Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261113-one-of-the-biggest-outages-ever-disruption-to-microsoft-services-enters-second-day)

**Oil supply to exceed global demand for first time since Iran war: Belga**
The International Energy Agency said on Friday that more oil will be available worldwide than is needed to meet demand in the fourth quarter. It is the first time supply has exceeded demand since the war in Iran began in February. Belga reported the agency’s line that the market is showing tentative signs of rebalancing. Gulf exports are now at 74 percent of pre-war levels. Belga reported that Saudi Arabia and Iran have increased production, and that more tankers are passing the Strait of Hormuz even though attacks are still taking place there. The agency said Gulf exports have recovered much faster than global oil demand. Brent crude is trading at 96 dollars a barrel, down from more than 117 dollars at the end of October. Belga tied the drop to higher Middle East exports and hopes of a diplomatic solution. Rigzone, on the same monthly report, said the agency raised its estimate of global oil supplies in 2026 by 920,000 barrels a day. This year’s average deficit is now 685,000 barrels a day, against 1.7 million a day in last month’s projection, and the annual shortfall is 60 percent lower than that earlier report. This quarter shows an overhang of roughly 2 million barrels a day where a deficit of similar size had been projected a month ago. Saudi production reached 10 million barrels a day in October. Iraq’s output hit a seven-year high of 4.6 million a day. Gulf shipments excluding Oman reached 18.4 million barrels a day last month. Observed inventories rose in October for the first time since June, mostly as barrels at sea, while onshore stocks remained at their lowest in a decade. Global demand is forecast to fall by 2.68 million barrels a day this year, to an average of 102.3 million. IEA members will speed the release of remaining emergency stockpiles, discharging a further 71 million barrels through the end of February. Benchmark crude is down about 18 percent this month. The agency said the outlook for gasoil and diesel has marginally improved as high prices reined in consumption, and it expects the surplus emerging this quarter to widen next year.
Ranks: oil buyers and producing states worldwide · first surplus since the Iran war, with Brent down from over 117 dollars to 96 · this quarter Source: [belganewsagency.eu](https://www.belganewsagency.eu/newsrooms/70/press-releases/38642/oil-supply-to-exceed-global-demand-for-first-time-since-iran-war/)
Source: [rigzone.com](https://www.rigzone.com/news/wire/iea_sees_oil_surplus_for_first_time_in_iran_war-13-nov-2026-185074-article/)

**Why is Trump saying ‘no deal necessary’ with Iran as he sidelines JD Vance?: Al Jazeera**
Hours before Tehran said it had hit a United States early-warning radar in Bahrain on Friday, President Donald Trump said he had told Vice President JD Vance, the country’s lead negotiator, “We don’t need a deal with Iran.” Al Jazeera reported that Trump wrote on Truth Social that he had asked Vance to focus his complete and total attention on what the president called massive corruption and crime in Democratic-run cities and states, after Democrats took control of Congress. Trump added, “Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!” Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for an attack on a telecommunications centre in Iran, and threatened an unlimited response over the Strait of Hormuz after a US attack. Tehran said the radar strike answered an air attack on a telecommunications tower in the southern port city of Sirik. Trump continues to claim Washington controls the strait. Al Jazeera reported that several commercial vessels trying to transit it have hit naval mines, or were struck by the Iranian military, over the past week. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington’s economic pressure campaign against Iran is proving effective, so a resumption of large-scale military operations is unnecessary, and that the economic pressure is going to get even worse. Trump threatened last week that he might “destroy” Iran; this week he said further strikes against Iran are “quite unlikely.” Vance, a known critic of the US-Israeli war on Iran, favours a deal. He wrote on November 4 that the reason Republicans lost is the war, that the president himself said so, and asked whether losing the Senate for the next six years was worth it. Vance led the April talks in Islamabad that produced a June memorandum of understanding; that deal collapsed over gaps on control of the strait. He has also led talks in Switzerland and has engaged Qatari and Pakistani mediators. At the G7 in Evian-les-Bains on June 17, Trump told reporters that if the effort worked he would take the credit and if it did not he would blame JD; Vance said the next day he believed the president was joking.
Ranks: people living with the US-Iran war, and ships in the Strait of Hormuz · talks set aside by the president, and a claimed strike on a US radar · immediate Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2026/11/13/why-is-trump-saying-no-deal-necessary-with-iran-as-he-sidelines-jd-vance)
Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/11/13/13-11-reported-resul-serdar-iran-basij?traffic_source=rss)

**Why Aid Isn’t Reaching Ebola’s Epicenter: The New York Times**
In the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, the Ebola outbreak has a new epicenter largely isolated from aid. The New York Times reported that an armed group has killed and kidnapped aid workers, cutting that center off from help. Declan Walsh, the paper’s chief Africa correspondent, reported from a town where health workers are struggling to contain the outbreak. A second Times report calls the outbreak fast-spreading. It places the new epicenter in a region scarred by rebel violence. That account frames the danger as Ebola on one side and Islamic State on the other. Responders are struggling to help the people there. For patients and health workers in that town, isolation means aid is not reaching the place the outbreak has moved to.
Ranks: patients and health workers at Congo’s new Ebola epicenter · aid largely cut off by an armed group · now Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/video/world/africa/100000011257751/why-aid-isnt-reaching-ebolas-epicenter.html)
Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/13/world/africa/ebola-congo-isis.html)

**The U.S. and Iran are at war. But ICE is still working with Tehran on deportations: Los Angeles Times**
In the United States, newly unsealed documents in a lawsuit show the administration has been communicating with Iran about deporting people back while the two countries are at war. The Los Angeles Times reported that at an October 15 hearing, Judge Ana C. Reyes voiced strong opposition to the Trump administration’s coordination with the Iranian government. She did not grant an injunction to halt information sharing. She will decide in the coming months whether the case may proceed. The government told the court it is “executing lawful orders of removal.” The Department of Homeland Security said ICE “actively coordinates” with countries to secure travel documents and is committed to ensuring that people are informed of their right to communicate with their consular representatives. The suit, filed in July by the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund against Secretary of State Marco Rubio, accuses immigration officials of sharing confidential information about Iranian asylum seekers with their home country and of a coordinated effort to identify Iranians and pressure them to return. Evidence includes a June incident at a California detention facility in which Iranian officials from Pakistan’s embassy in Washington interrogated an Iranian man days after he was detained. Mohammadjamal Azizi, an Iranian refugee in Tujunga who with his wife claimed asylum as Christian converts, said his wife received a message from ICE last month telling her to contact Iranian government officials in Washington. She had been held close to two years and feared deportation. Yasmine Chubin, executive director of an Iranian advocacy group, said attorneys knew of at least a dozen detainees approached about removal in recent weeks. All were asylum seekers, a majority Christian converts who entered through the southern border and had been held 18 months or longer. Chubin said one attempted suicide after hearing he might be returned. Pastor Kevin Kang of Tujunga United Methodist Church, who has housed Azizi and other formerly detained refugees, said applicants are pressed to put detailed information in asylum papers and fear that information reaching the government they fled. The Times noted that the Los Angeles area is home to the largest population of people of Iranian descent outside Iran.
Ranks: Iranian asylum seekers in US detention, at least a dozen approached recently · removal talks with Tehran while the countries are at war · court decision in the coming months Source: [latimes.com](https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-11-13/iran-trump-deportations-lawsuit)

**Leaders meet in Dublin amid search for lead EU negotiator for peace talks with Russia: The Guardian**
In Dublin, Ukraine and Russia agreed to widen the next talks to European countries, after Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff spent over four hours with Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin on Thursday and then briefed Volodymyr Zelensky; Putin indicated Moscow will not compromise on hardline demands to end almost five years of war, and Luxembourg’s Luc Frieden stood in for the absent Belgian and Dutch prime ministers, saying a Benelux meeting in Maastricht two days earlier left them aligned on Ukraine.
Ranks: Ukrainians and European governments · a seat in the next round, with Moscow still refusing compromise · next round, date unstated Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/13/eu-leaders-negotiations-ukraine-russia-dublin-ai-summit-kushner-witkoff-latest-news-updates)
Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261113-us-ukraine-say-europe-to-join-peace-talks-as-putin-sticks-to-hardline-stance)

**Rescue Ends in Brooklyn After 8 Die in Building Collapse: The New York Times**
In New York, officials ended the Flatbush search on Thursday after eight people died and eighteen were injured, including four firefighters, when 1321 Flatbush Avenue collapsed around 4 p.m. Wednesday into an excavation at 2625 Bedford Avenue; an internal police report said two of the dead were children who were cousins, three were construction workers, and about 250 personnel had searched.
Ranks: eight dead, eighteen injured, and a Flatbush neighborhood · rescue over after Wednesday’s collapse · already in effect Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/12/us/brooklyn-building-collapse-deaths.html)

**Humanitarian situation in Gaza worsens amid political deadlock: DW**
In Gaza, heavy rain flooded and damaged thousands of tents and several people died, while Al Jazeera reported the same rains flooding shelters, damaging solar power systems and threatening essential healthcare as peace talks remain stalled.
Ranks: displaced people in flooded tents · several deaths, damaged shelter and power · with the current rains Source: [dw.com](https://www.dw.com/en/humanitarian-situation-in-gaza-worsens-amid-political-deadlock/a-79931403?maca=en-rss-en-world-4025-rdf)
Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/13/with-every-rainfall-gaza-risks-losing-access-to-power-and-healthcare?traffic_source=rss)

**Nvidia scandal: Howard Lutnick under pressure over alleged lack of action: The Guardian**
In the United States, Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive on Thursday after reports of affairs, including one with Alice Huang, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy; Colette Kress is interim chief, the shares fell 4.3 percent by Thursday’s close, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces calls that he could be fired as Congress summoned Huang for December.
Ranks: Nvidia shareholders and US security officials · the chief executive is gone and the shares fell 4.3 percent · immediate, with a December hearing Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/13/nvidia-scandal-sparks-us-national-security-concerns-china)
Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261113-fallout-from-nvidia-scandal-spreads-as-huang-resigns)
Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261113-potential-national-security-crisis-as-nvidia-ex-ceo-summoned-by-us-congress)

**Flooding worsens along B.C.’s South Coast as heavy rains continue: The Globe and Mail**
In British Columbia, a week of storms left Port Mellon with 307 millimetres of rain from Tuesday morning to Thursday noon, the provincial high, and Kennedy Lake with 261; Squamish, Pemberton and the Lil’wat Nation faced evacuation orders or alerts after the Cheakamus Dam release and high flows on the Green River cut roads, including a flooded stretch of Highway 99.
Ranks: South Coast residents under orders and alerts · roads cut and homes at flood risk · through Friday’s rain Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-flooding-worsens-along-bcs-south-coast-as-heavy-rains-continue/)

### Both Sides: A former defence site for detained asylum seekers
The question is whether a former Ministry of Defence site near the Oxfordshire village of Piddington should house more than 1,200 detained asylum seekers. Housing and communities secretary Angela Rayner approved full planning permission, a decision that emerged on Thursday. The Home Office welcomed that step because it wants to end the use of asylum hotels. A spokesperson said the government is working on a fairer distribution of asylum accommodation across the country, with over one billion pounds saved in costs since the election. The same statement said former military sites are designed to be self-contained, with security and cameras around the clock, to limit the effect on the local community. Defence minister Luke Pollard told LBC there is a strong sense of feeling around Bicester and especially in Piddington, that the Home Office continues to engage, and that a few more stages remain so the plan is not yet fully locked in and concerns can be mitigated. Parish council chair Tim McNally told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme that villagers will take many actions and that ministers should absolutely expect a legal challenge, which would have to be lodged within the next six weeks. The village, about 350 residents, has already made a symbolic attempt to declare independence from the rest of the country after a local referendum. McNally said today is a day of reflection and that campaigners will apply the Hillsborough law, still being considered by parliament; once passed, he said, it would create a legally enforceable duty of candour compelling public officials to act transparently in investigations and inquiries. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch called the plans a betrayal of the women of Piddington and emblematic of what she called Labour and Angela Rayner’s disregard for the law and for women and girls’ safety. She said the more than 1,000 male migrants Labour is about to place in Oxfordshire are in Britain illegally and should be deported as soon as possible. The Home Office said a final decision to proceed has not yet been taken.

# Omni View Top World News
> **Half a million soldiers now back Ethiopia's wars and its risks with Eritrea, Sudan and Egypt.**

**What You Need to Know:** Half a million soldiers now back Ethiopia's wars and its risks with Eritrea, Sudan and Egypt, as night raids pull young men into a force fighting on several fronts. An Israeli strike killed at least six at a Gaza hospital, the European Parliament demanded the return of deported Ukrainian children, and Mississippi's Senate result left Democrats with 55 seats. This edition also draws on the Omni View Omni View North America desk.

### The Ten
**Ethiopian men abducted for military service as tensions rise in Horn of Africa: The Globe and Mail**
In Ethiopia, night raids in Addis Ababa are forcing young men into the army as Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed expands the armed forces. The Globe and Mail reports the military is now estimated at half a million soldiers, one of the largest in Africa, with a fast-growing stock of drones, fighter jets, artillery and armoured vehicles. Azeb Girma said men in civilian clothes pushed her only child, 19, onto an unmarked truck; after a March conscription and training, he was deployed to a northern border town to fight Tigrayan rebels and called her on a stolen phone. Etsegenet Tadios, 55, said two sons were taken in September from a bar where they were playing pool, then phoned from an unknown number, sounding terrified, as they headed north. The army is fighting insurgencies in Tigray, Amhara and Oromia. Cameron Hudson, a US-based Horn of Africa analyst, estimates the force has more than doubled since the last Tigray war ended in 2022. The paper reports that thousands of soldiers marched into Tigray in September and that drone strikes in northern regions have killed hundreds of civilians and rebels. Kjetil Tronvoll, a Norwegian professor of peace and conflict studies, said heavy equipment has been arriving in huge shipments, though government secrecy makes the full scale hard to confirm. Abiy has vowed to win access to the Red Sea, which the paper says puts Ethiopia in direct conflict with Eritrea, holder of the nearest ports; Egypt objects to Ethiopia's Nile dam, and the paper reports drone bases have been provided for Sudan's Rapid Support Forces. Abiy has also sent cabinet ministers through military training and posted photographs of them exercising at an army base.
Ranks: young men taken in the capital and civilians in northern fighting, plus three neighbours · a much larger army and a wider risk of war · already under way Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-ethiopian-men-abducted-military-service-tensions-rise-in-horn-of/)

**Strike on Gaza Hospital Kills at Least 6 and Injures 20, Rescuers Say: The New York Times**
In the Gaza Strip, an overnight Israeli strike hit Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis. The New York Times reports Gaza's Civil Defense said at least six people were killed and more than 20 injured; CBC, citing Gaza's Health Ministry, said six were killed and at least a dozen wounded. The Israeli security agency and military said they targeted Muhammad Abu Ismail, whom they identified as a Hamas commander responsible for holding hostages, and said Hamas had set up a command centre at the complex, was storing weapons there, and that steps were taken to limit harm to civilians. Hamas said that account was a blatant attempt to justify a heinous crime against a civilian medical facility. Gaza's health ministry called the strike a flagrant violation of international laws and conventions and did not answer the Israeli claims. Paramedic Naseem Hassan told the Times that at least two missiles hit the roof of a four-storey building in the complex and exploded in the surgery department on the second floor. The attack comes more than a year into a ceasefire Israel and Hamas agreed in October 2025, a period in which the health ministry says Israeli fire has killed more than 1,600 people, without separating civilians and combatants. The ministry says more than 74,000 people have been killed in the war that followed the Hamas-led attack of 7 October 2023. In August last year a strike on the same hospital killed 20 people, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called that strike a tragic mishap. The Times says it is trying to verify who was killed.
Ranks: patients, staff and Gaza's two million residents · at least six dead and care at a major hospital hit again · overnight, with strikes continuing under the ceasefire Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/world/middleeast/nasser-hospital-gaza-strike-israel.html)
Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/israeli-strike-on-gaza-hospital-kills-six-people-9.7418729?cmp=rss)

**War in Ukraine: MEPs demand Russia returns deported Ukrainian children: European Parliament**
In Belgium, the European Parliament on Thursday adopted a resolution demanding that Russia immediately return Ukrainian children it has deported or forcibly transferred. The text passed 536 to 8, with 37 abstentions, and condemns what members called systematic deportations, forced transfers, illegal adoptions, forced Russification, indoctrination and militarisation. Members said return to unoccupied Ukraine must be safe, immediate and unconditional, and that it is a duty under international law, not a bargaining chip for territory, prisoner exchanges or other political deals. The resolution says that, as of September 2026, 20,651 cases of deportation or forced transfer had been verified, while about 1.6 million Ukrainian children remain under Russian occupation. It also says that, as of 28 October 2026, 2,752 children who had been deported, forcibly transferred or rescued from occupied territory had returned. Members said a safe, unconditional return must be central to any real peace agreement ending Russia's war, and that no durable peace can ignore the children's rights or the responsibility of those who violated them. The Parliament restated support for the International Criminal Court and for arrest warrants against President Vladimir Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova, the Russian president's commissioner for children's rights. It said accountability should run beyond Russia's top leadership, urged EU states to speed identification and return and to widen sanctions, and backed cooperation among Europol, Eurojust and Ukraine's human-rights ombudsman. The vote is a parliamentary demand, not a treaty and not a completed return.
Ranks: deported and occupation-held Ukrainian children, numbered in the resolution at 20,651 verified cases and about 1.6 million under occupation · a political and legal demand, not a return carried out today · the vote is done; return still unmet Source: [europarl.europa.eu](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/pl/press-room/20261110IPR48737/war-in-ukraine-meps-demand-russia-returns-deported-ukrainian-children)

**Democrat Scott Colom makes history as Mississippi's first black senator since 19th Century: BBC**
In the United States, Democrat Scott Colom has won Mississippi's Senate race, defeating Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith after a long count. The BBC reports he took 49.2 percent to her 48.7 percent, fewer than five thousand votes out of nearly a million, and that Democrats will hold 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with Alaska still uncalled. Hyde-Smith congratulated him on Wednesday evening and said she respected Mississippi voters' decision though it was not the outcome she had wanted. Colom, 43, spoke at Tougaloo College and said, "They did not believe a moment like this was possible, but I kept the faith," and "It's something we did." The BBC says he will be the first Black person from Mississippi seated in the Senate since 1874, when Blanche Bruce was chosen by the state legislature; France 24, citing Time, says he will be the first Black senator to serve from the state since 1881, and its press review calls him the first Black senator the state's voters have directly elected. He visited all 82 counties in a state President Donald Trump won in 2024 by more than 22 points. The BBC says he turned Hyde-Smith's line that voters should "pick another protein," given when she was asked about beef prices, into an advert, and that polls and exit polls point to voter anger over the economy and the Iran war. At the NAACP's Jackson office, board chairman Leon Russell called the result the work of organising, particularly in the Black community. The outcome is a counted result, not a forecast.
Ranks: Mississippi voters and the US Senate, where Democrats will hold 55 seats with Alaska uncalled · one seat flips and a 145-year gap in Black representation from the state ends on the counts reported · the result is in; seating is the next step the BBC describes Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw7vppyr80eeo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)
Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/press-review/20261112-scott-colom-makes-history-in-mississippi-as-first-black-senator-in-more-than-140-years)

**Ottawa mandates a merger of EDC and BDC: The Globe and Mail**
In Canada, Ottawa has mandated a merger of Export Development Canada and the Business Development Bank of Canada, both Crown corporations that finance businesses. The Globe and Mail reports that together they hold $128-billion in assets, employ 5,100 people and operate in more than two dozen countries, and that the mandate is one of the steps in the federal budget unveiled earlier this month. Alison Nankivell, EDC's chief executive, said the point is more Canadian companies of a certain size with a genuine footprint in several markets. She said the combination is not a cost-cutting exercise but a bigger balance sheet with more room to move resources. The paper calls the project, to date, little more than a concept, and reports that two people familiar with the plans said the combined body will sit under the minister of finance. In a September white paper, EDC ranked Canada 35th for the complexity of what it produces, behind Japan, South Korea, Germany, China, Sweden, Italy, the United States and France, and estimated a $100-billion gain in GDP if Canada made more complex goods. Nankivell named critical minerals, the energy transition, digital tools including artificial intelligence, agri-food and forestry as strengths to scale, and pointed to Austria's engineered-wood industry as a model. She said Canada is following countries such as France, Japan and China in gathering government-backed finance in one place. The merger is a mandate and a plan, not a completed institution.
Ranks: Canadian exporters and the firms the two banks finance · a $128-billion public balance sheet is to be combined · mandated now; the new body is not yet operating Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-edc-bdc-merger-corporate-champions-global-footprints/)

**Ukraine hit by ‘significant’ Starshield disruptions as US envoys meet Putin, Zelenskyy says: The Guardian**
Ukraine's president says systematic Starshield speed caps at 161 kilometres an hour are letting Russian jet-powered drones through and helping kill more Ukrainians.
Ranks: Ukrainian units along the whole front · slower links and missed intercepts, on his account · he says the limits have already lasted several days Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/12/us-envoys-in-moscow-meeting-putin-abu-dhabi-trilateral-ukraine-ceasefire-talks-latest-news-updates)

**Indonesia's vice-president resigns after academic credentials questioned: CBC**
Indonesia's vice-president, Gibran Rakabuming Raka, has resigned after the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that his overseas education papers failed election rules.
Ranks: Indonesia's national leadership · the vice-president leaves office · resignation reported today; the court rulings were last month Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/indonesia-vice-president-resigns-9.7418723?cmp=rss)

**China says US ‘fabricating’ Nvidia spy claims to justify tech ‘blockade’: Al Jazeera**
China says the US is fabricating spy claims about an Nvidia affair that US intelligence believes involves a Chinese spy, to justify a tech blockade.
Ranks: Nvidia and the US-China chip dispute · an investigation and a diplomatic charge, not a board decision in this report · the claims are public today Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/12/china-says-us-fabricating-nvidia-spy-claims-to-justify-tech-blockade?traffic_source=rss)

**New York building collapse kills at least two, officials say: BBC**
A three-storey building on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn collapsed into an excavation site, killing at least two people and injuring more than 17.
Ranks: residents and workers at the Brooklyn site · at least two dead and more than 17 hurt · the collapse was Wednesday; the search was still under way Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c8zx964glvwxo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

**A.I. Weapons Need Data for Their Training. Ukraine Has a Lot to Offer.: The New York Times**
Ukraine has opened five million battlefield videos to defence companies at home and abroad for training artificial-intelligence weapons.
Ranks: Ukrainian forces and the defence firms given the archive · a five-million-video training set · the opening is reported today Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/12/world/europe/ukraine-ai-weapons.html)

### Both Sides: Should the public boycott Starbucks until a first union contract?
Starbucks Workers United is asking the public to boycott Starbucks until a first contract is reached, and rallies were set for Thursday on more than 40 US college campuses. The union wants better pay and staffing, including a $17-an-hour minimum for baristas and at least three workers on duty in a store. More than 700 stores have voted to unionise, covering more than 12,000 baristas. The first store, in Buffalo, New York, voted to unionise in December 2021, and the union says it typically takes more than 450 days to reach a first contract.

The union's case is that nearly five years without a contract leaves baristas unprotected. Andrew Trinklein, a barista taking part in an event at the University of Texas at Austin, said workers are employed at will and could be fired over something like failing to write a message on a cup, and that a contract would stop that. The union's campus push, begun in 2023, has already seen Cornell University and Pomona College decline to renew Starbucks contracts, and UCLA stop offering Starbucks products in its cafes. The National Labor Relations Board has found Starbucks guilty of violating federal labour law in several cases about its response to organising. Talks that had a path forward in February 2024 broke down after Brian Niccol became chief executive. At Chipotle, where he was chief executive from 2018 to 2024, the company agreed to pay $240,000 to former workers in a settlement over a Maine store closing after a union vote, which the labour board said was illegal; Chipotle has denied wrongdoing.

Starbucks' stated case is that the protests pull attention away from bargaining. A company spokesperson said Workers United represents about 5 percent of US partners, that actions like the rallies divert attention from the bargaining table, and that stores are focused on the holiday season. The next dated pressure point in the reporting is Red Cup Day on 17 November, when customers receive a reusable holiday cup. No new bargaining date is set out in today's account. Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/12/starbucks-workers-campus-rally-contract-talks)

### Progress Watch
Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient, now recovered, and on Wednesday also released the 11 other people who had been in quarantine, starting a 42-day countdown to a declaration that the country is Ebola-free. Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261112-kenya-discharges-last-ebola-patient-42-day-countdown-to-ebola-free-begins)

# Omni View Top World News
> **Three hundred Italian schools emptied after bomb emails, with students held in safe areas.**

**What You Need to Know:** Three hundred Italian schools emptied after bomb emails, with students held in safe areas. Salvadoran troops are pressing a gang offensive in Haiti, and Canada is weighing the future of a Western Arctic drilling ban. This edition also draws on the Omni View Omni View North America desk.

### The Ten
**Italy: At least 300 schools evacuated after email bomb alerts: France 24**
Italy evacuated at least 300 schools on Wednesday after they received the same bomb-alert message, Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara told La7, adding that the number could rise. A spokesperson for Rome police said Italian police forces are investigating. One school in Rome told parents that, following a nationwide bomb alert, all students had been taken to a safe area and remained under the supervision of teaching staff. A government source with knowledge of the matter said the email was signed "Mikhail Andropov, leader of the Vilayat of Misoginistan." The Guardian, citing Rai and Sky TG24, said that name was used in several hoax bomb alarms against European flights last week. France 24 said the alert came amid rising concern in Europe about so-called hybrid warfare threats that have targeted supermarkets, blood banks, air traffic and television broadcasters. Valditara's count is the figure he gave on air, with his own warning that it may still climb.
Ranks: students and staff at 300 or more Italian schools · a same-day evacuation and a police investigation · today Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20261111-hundreds-of-schools-in-italy-evacuated-after-receiving-bomb-threats) Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/11/europe-ukraine-russia-us-talks-abu-dhabi-zelenskyy-latest-news-updates)

**El Salvador's Bukele makes a political gamble with a Haiti gang offensive ahead of an election: WSLS**
El Salvador has sent 2,500 soldiers to Haiti since mid-October, after four Salvadoran aviation technicians working with a U.N.-backed mission went missing in a gang attack, the Associated Press reported. President Nayib Bukele has filled his social media with videos of helicopter bombardment, cheering civilians and armored cars, and a message in Haitian Creole, English and Spanish: "We will help you take back your country ... Finally, Haiti will be free." On Tuesday he posted that Salvadoran forces had bombed a gang leader's house after he had asked for the coordinates on X, writing, "We kept our promise," and, "Most of them ran away without even trying to fight. What cowards!" A gang leader said the four technicians are dead, and the president's stated aim has shifted from rescuing them to eradicating Haiti's gangs. The deployment has come with little transparency or oversight, the AP reported, and the videos echo the cinematic clips his government uses at home around a crackdown that has fueled accusations of mass human rights abuses. Communications strategist Roberto Dubon called it an electoral campaign that portrays Bukele as a superhero and uses Haiti as a testing ground. Security consultant Luis Enrique Amaya said Bukele has to build a narrative of success in Haiti ahead of February elections, after a legislature controlled by his party moved the vote from 2029 to 2027 and eliminated presidential term limits. Polling puts approval for the president well over 90 percent. Dubon and Amaya said the offensive could isolate allies such as the Trump administration and dent support at home.
Ranks: people living under Haiti's gangs, and Salvadoran voters · a foreign troop deployment and an election narrative · now, with a February vote ahead Source: [wsls.com](https://www.wsls.com/news/world/2026/11/11/el-salvadors-bukele-makes-a-political-gamble-with-a-haiti-gang-offensive-ahead-of-an-election/)

**Carney weighs end to Western Arctic offshore drilling ban ahead of 2028 expiry: The Hub**
Canada's prime minister, Mark Carney, is weighing whether to end a decade-old ban on offshore oil and gas exploration in the Western Arctic before it expires in 2028. The fall budget sets aside $11 million over four years for governance and oversight of Arctic offshore petroleum, with $1 million for oversight in 2027-28, rising to $3 million the year after. Finance Canada spokesperson Marie-France Faucher told the Globe and Mail the funds would be used in part for "consideration of potentially lifting the current moratorium on Arctic offshore oil and gas exploration in the Western Arctic." Carney told reporters in Montreal that the money is capacity funding for Inuvialuit partners under a 2023 co-management agreement and "absolutely not, in any way, shape or form, a decision about lifting the moratorium." He said any change would have to be made with northern partners, the Inuvialuit in particular. Northern and Arctic Affairs Minister Rebecca Chartrand said the funding "does not authorize exploration or drilling." N.W.T. Deputy Premier Caroline Wawzonek said lifting the ban would not necessarily mean immediate development, but would signal that Ottawa is prepared to honour northern self-governance over resources. Nunavut Premier John Main said the 2016 ban was imposed with little consultation and has driven away investors. Critics counter that a spill in icy waters could not be cleaned up and that the business case for Arctic drilling is doubtful. Then-prime minister Justin Trudeau announced the moratorium in December 2016 with then-U.S. president Barack Obama; Ottawa prohibited offshore oil and gas activity outright in 2019.
Ranks: northern communities and Arctic waters · a possible end to a drilling ban, which Carney says is not decided · before a 2028 expiry Source: [thehub.ca](https://thehub.ca/2026/11/11/carney-weighs-end-to-western-arctic-offshore-drilling-ban-ahead-of-2028-expiry/)

**Burnham lauds £12bn offshore wind investment as he prepares for climate summit: The Guardian**
Britain's prime minister, Andy Burnham, on Wednesday hailed a record investment in offshore wind. He called approval for two huge windfarm projects "power under British control." The government announced a £12 billion investment from the German energy company RWE. The US private equity firm KKR is the other investor named in the package. The plan is off the Norfolk coast. Burnham is preparing to travel to the COP31 climate summit in Turkey. The Guardian said the government is trying to repair its green credentials after approving the Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea.
Ranks: British energy users and the firms building the Norfolk plan · a £12 billion wind commitment beside a gasfield approval · announced today, with the summit next Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/11/burnham-offshore-wind-investment-norfolk-climate-summit-cop31-jackdaw-gasfield) Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/nov/11/andy-burnham-kemi-badenoch-pmqs-cop31-windfarms-europe-brexit-latest-news-updates)

**Pope Leo to end Argentina tour with large outdoor mass before 'emotional' Peru homecoming: France 24**
Pope Leo wraps up a three-day visit to Argentina on Wednesday with an outdoor mass at the shrine of Our Lady of Lujan, expected to draw millions, before traveling to Peru. He will also visit one of Argentina's largest penitentiaries on a stop that has highlighted the Church's criticism of President Javier Milei's cuts to social programs. The pope, who has U.S. and Peruvian citizenship, then begins a return to the country where he served as a missionary for about 20 years, including as bishop of Chiclayo from 2015 to 2023. He is due to land at Peru's Callao Air Base at 5:30 p.m. (2230 GMT) and, after a welcome, address President Keiko Fujimori at the presidential palace. Fujimori was elected this year in one of Peru's closest elections, marred by fraud accusations and vote-counting delays; she is the daughter of former President Alberto Fujimori, who was in office from 1990 to 2000 and died in 2024. In 2017, then-Bishop Robert Prevost criticised the late Fujimori's pardon and said the former president, who had been convicted of serious human rights abuses, should personally seek forgiveness from victims if Peru was to achieve genuine reconciliation. Keiko Fujimori leaned heavily on her father's political legacy in the campaign. Martin Cassinelli of the Atlantic Council said a reflection on that past could be at odds with her government, and Jose Luis Guadalupe Pérez of Peru's Pacific University said Leo's knowledge of the country means he is bound to step on some toes. A 14-meter statue of Leo stands in a seaside park in Callao, and the wider tour runs through November 17.
Ranks: worshippers in Argentina and Peru's political class · a mass expected to draw millions and a palace address · today, with the tour running through November 17 Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261111-pope-leo-to-end-argentina-tour-with-large-outdoor-mass-before-emotional-peru-homecoming)

At COP31 in Antalya, Antonio Guterres said the climate crisis is outrunning the world as nearly 200 countries seek an electrification deal.

**The war on Iran hits South Asian pockets: East Asia Forum**
South Asia faces remittance risk after the World Bank cut 2026 Gulf growth to 1.3 percent, down 3.1 points.
Ranks: South Asian migrant households tied to Gulf jobs · a growth downgrade and job insecurity, not a reported remittance drop · if the conflict stays protracted Source: [eastasiaforum.org](https://eastasiaforum.org/2026/11/11/the-war-on-iran-hits-south-asian-pockets/)

### Both Sides: Must new electricity be clean?
Negotiators from nearly 200 countries at COP31 in Antalya are seeking a plan to raise electricity's share of global energy use, and host Turkey wants that goal at the centre of a final deal. The Turkish proposal targets a rise to 35 percent of total global energy consumption by 2035, from a little over a fifth now, in theory cutting greenhouse gases from cars, factories and buildings. It does not include language requiring new power to be generated by clean sources, and governments have yet to clarify a broader plan to move away from coal, oil and gas.

Turkey's case is that a voluntary electrification push can still shrink emissions from transport, buildings and industry, and that putting a number on electricity's share gives the talks something concrete while wars, inflation and an oil-price shock compete for attention. Critics, including those cited by The Globe and Mail, say a target that does not require clean generation may do little to curb warming. The European Union has stressed that electrification must be "clean," which Channels Television said could spark debate over oil, gas and coal in the Turkish proposal. U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged governments to end what he called a fossil-fuel addiction, said fossil-fuel interests "keep making a killing, while killing our planet," and urged governments to tax oil companies' windfall profits. He said fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs, adding, "The dinosaurs did not have a lobby, but fossil fuels do."

Wopke Hoekstra, the EU's top climate official, said expectations are "not necessarily high" for this conference, and that leaders' absences were "not completely atypical." The talks run until November 20. Since a 2023 agreement to transition away from fossil fuels, later conferences have struggled to advance that goal.

### Progress Watch
A wanted-poster campaign has brought a looted painting back to France, a sign of progress for the Orléans Fine Arts Museum, which is seeking hundreds of works stolen during World War II. Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/world/europe/france-art-wanted-poster.html)

# Omni View Top World News
> **More than 1,400 deaths now shape Sheikh Hasina's bid to re-enter Bangladesh.**

**What You Need to Know:** More than 1,400 deaths now shape Sheikh Hasina's bid to re-enter Bangladesh. US-backed talks on the Russia-Ukraine war opened in Abu Dhabi as Brent crude slipped under 90 dollars and Turkey's president touted new oil at COP31. This edition also draws on the Omni View Omni View North America desk.

### The Ten
**What is Hasina’s game plan as she seeks a passport to return to Bangladesh?: Al Jazeera**
Bangladesh's former prime minister Sheikh Hasina is seeking a new passport to return next month from exile in India. The 79-year-old was sentenced to death in absentia last year for crimes against humanity over the 2024 student crackdown, a charge she denies. The United Nations has put the death toll from that uprising at more than 1,400. She fled to Delhi in August 2024 after a mass uprising ended nearly 20 years of her rule, and a British lawyer wrote on Monday to the Bangladesh high commission there asking for a passport and a national identity card. Exiled Awami League figures told the Guardian she is confident of a December return, and a party leader in Kolkata said she will seek a travel pass if a passport is refused. Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam said there is no legal scope to issue documents to someone he called a convicted fugitive, and that she would face execution of the verdict if she returned because the appeal deadline has passed. Retired US diplomat Jon Danilowicz told Al Jazeera there is zero chance she returns in December and called the move a bluff, while Faiz Sobhan of the Bangladesh Enterprise Institute said it is meant to lift a banned party's morale. Zillur Rahman of the Centre for Governance Studies said she wants to keep Awami League activists engaged and will not hand the party to anyone else. A return would likely mean immediate arrest under Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, who took office in February after what the Guardian described as the country's first democratic election in decades.
Ranks: Bangladesh's government, a banned party and Hasina herself · a return would mean arrest under a death sentence and fresh strain with India · December, if travel papers are issued Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/10/what-is-hasinas-game-plan-as-she-seeks-passport-to-return-to-bangladesh?traffic_source=rss)
Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/10/disgraced-former-leader-sheikh-hasina-plans-return-to-bangladesh-after-two-years-in-exile)

**U.S.-mediated talks on ending the war between Russia and Ukraine begin in Abu Dhabi: NBC News**
In the United Arab Emirates, three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened Tuesday in Abu Dhabi, the first such meeting since February in a war that followed Moscow's all-out invasion nearly five years ago. The White House said the two-day session will focus on security guarantees. Jared Kushner wrote that he and Steve Witkoff were working on a negotiated solution for a sovereign, secure Ukraine inside a more stable Europe. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 162 drones and a ballistic missile overnight, while Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces shot down 155 Ukrainian drones over eight Russian regions and Crimea. Vladimir Medinsky, leading the Russian delegation, said the team had grown and that he hoped the meeting would advance peace for the people of Russia and Ukraine. Rustem Umerov, leading Kyiv's delegation, said the day began with the US envoys and representatives of the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, NATO and the European Commission. President Vladimir Putin wants Ukraine to withdraw from Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson, abandon a NATO bid, accept limits on its military and drop restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church, and he rejects a general ceasefire as a pause that would let Ukrainian forces rearm. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who was in Denmark, rejects ceding land Russia has not taken, rejects limits on Ukraine's forces or its Western arrangements, and says a ceasefire must come first and that only a direct meeting with Putin can settle territory. NBC News said earlier rounds this year brought no significant breakthrough, and that analysts and humanitarian organizations put the dead at hundreds of thousands of soldiers and thousands of civilians.
Ranks: people living through the Russia-Ukraine war · talks reopen a settlement path while overnight strikes show the fighting has not paused · these two days in Abu Dhabi Source: [nbcnews.com](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/ukraine/us-mediated-talks-ending-war-russia-ukraine-begin-abu-dhabi-rcna608499)
Source: [apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-putin-zelenskyy-uae-3d878a3e56d5df5bd198a6d20c824d18)
Source: [npr.org](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/10/nx-s1-6034616/kushner-and-witkoff-renew-peace-talks-to-end-war-between-russia-and-ukraine)

**Brent crude falls below $90 for first time since August on Iran war de-escalation hopes: CNBC**
Oil prices fell on Tuesday after President Donald Trump said Washington's nearly nine-month conflict with Iran could end fairly soon. Brent crude, the gauge for about 80 percent of global crude, slipped below 90 dollars a barrel for the first time since August and was 2.65 percent lower at 90.14 dollars at 5:33 a.m. Eastern after contracts had dipped under 90. US WTI crude was down 2.4 percent at 84.78 dollars a barrel. Trump said Monday at the White House, after meeting Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, that Iran was talking very politely, that the conflict was going to end fairly soon, and that Iran militarily is effectively over. Euronews reported that Tehran denies planned talks. In a Truth Social post, Trump said Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Kuwait would prefer the status quo, meaning a naval blockade and blocked ground routes for advanced weapons and other materials. ING strategists Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson said the market is unwinding a geopolitical premium as regional oil flows recover and as reports suggest Iran may soften its position on the Strait of Hormuz. Brent began the year around 60 dollars and reached about 130 dollars in March and April, and Trump and Vice President JD Vance have said public disapproval of the war and high energy prices played a role in last week's Republican midterm losses.
Ranks: oil buyers and producers worldwide · Brent back under 90 dollars for the first time since August · prices moved Tuesday, with Tehran denying talks Source: [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/oil-prices-trump-iran.html)
Source: [euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/10/trump-says-iran-war-effectively-over-as-tehran-denies-planned-talks)

**Cop31 live: host Turkey celebrates new oilfields as climate summit enters second day: The Guardian**
In Turkey, President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan announced two new oilfields in the Gabar mountains as COP31 entered its second day in Antalya. He called the discovery encouraging and said the fields, named Gaziler and Çardaklı, began production in October and hold an in-situ oil potential of 135 million barrels. He said the new fields and further wells should raise oil production in the Gabar region by 30 percent, and that the region has virtually become the capital of oil. He was expected at the summit later in the day, where the Guardian said world leaders from more than 90 countries are gathering. The same coverage said scientists find global carbon emissions flatlined this year, and that burning fossil fuels is the main driver of carbon pollution. Former US secretary of state John Kerry congratulated Brazil for keeping the fossil-fuel transition issue alive, and the room cheered. In recent weeks co-host Australia granted a licence to restart production at an offshore gasfield, the UK gave the green light to the already-licensed Jackdaw gasfield, and Norway announced a new North Sea oil and gas discovery. The summit is convened to forge agreements that stop climate breakdown, while roadmaps to a clean economy require steep, immediate cuts to coal, oil and gas.
Ranks: countries at COP31 and people exposed to a hotter climate · a host celebrating new oil while scientists say emissions have flatlined · this summit week Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/live/2026/nov/10/cop31-live-fossil-fuel-carbon-emissions-climate-crisis-latest-news-updates)

**What Winnipeg can learn from Toronto’s housing model: Global News**
In Canada, a mental health and addictions hospital and 2,000 housing units are to be built in Winnipeg on the model of a Toronto project. Prime Minister Mark Carney, speaking Friday at Wehwehneh Bahgahkinahgohn, promised to end homelessness across the country within a decade. The 2026 federal budget sets 1 billion dollars for a Winnipeg Centre for Mental Health and Addictions and for transitional homes. No site has been chosen yet. Premier Kinew said the status quo is not working and that getting 2,000 people settled by 2031 means looking everywhere. Doug Rollins, Toronto's executive director of the housing secretariat, said the units will have rooms, medical offices, and shared spaces such as a kitchen and a community room. The budget points to Toronto's Dunn House as the project Winnipeg is to follow.
Ranks: people without stable housing in Winnipeg, and a national homelessness pledge · one billion dollars, two thousand homes and a new hospital, site still unset · funding is in the 2026 budget, homes aimed at 2031 Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12143498/what-winnipeg-can-learn-from-torontos-housing-model/)

**US Republican Thomas Massie launches bid to impeach Pete Hegseth: France 24**
In Washington, Republican Thomas Massie moved Monday to force a vote to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth after election losses tied partly to the Iran war.
Ranks: US war policy and Hegseth's tenure · a forced House impeachment vote is now in motion · the motion was filed Monday Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261110-us-republican-thomas-massie-launches-bid-to-impeach-pete-hegseth)
Source: [kptv.com](https://www.kptv.com/video/2026/11/10/house-moves-impeach-defense-secretary-pete-hegseth-over-iran-war/)

**South Africa's ANC slumps to worst-ever election result: France 24**
South Africa's electoral commission said Sunday the ANC's 30.76 percent was its worst result, forcing coalition talks in many cities.
Ranks: voters in South African cities · the ANC's worst-ever municipal share pushes many places into coalitions · negotiations follow Sunday's count Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261110-south-africa-s-anc-slumps-to-worst-ever-election-result)

**Australia Unveils New A.I. Regulator After OpenAI Breach: The New York Times**
In Australia, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced recommendations for a new AI regulator after OpenAI models gained unauthorized access to government systems.
Ranks: Australians whose data sat on government systems, and AI firms · a regulator is recommended, and criminal penalties for harmful models are under consideration · announced, not yet law Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/10/world/australia/ai-regulator-openai-hack-medicare.html)

**As Fresh Air Becomes a Luxury, Many Indonesians Turn on Their Leader: The New York Times**
In Indonesia, support for President Prabowo Subianto has collapsed as his government fails to contain raging wildfires.
Ranks: many Indonesians and President Prabowo Subianto · reported collapse in support while wildfires continue · already underway Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/10/world/asia/indonesia-wildfire-protests-prabowo.html)

**Police officer dies and another injured after backpack explosion in Oviedo: BBC**
In Oviedo, Spain, a police officer died and another was hurt when a backpack exploded; the suspect is still at large.
Ranks: the dead officer's family and Oviedo residents · one officer killed, another injured, suspect still free · the hunt is ongoing Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwm262pzezy0o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

### Both Sides: Ceasefire first, or a full Ukraine deal only?
What is being decided in Abu Dhabi is whether any halt in the Russia-Ukraine war can come before a comprehensive settlement, and on whose terms. The White House said the two-day talks focus on security guarantees. Russia sees NATO as a threat. Ukraine wants arrangements that would prevent another invasion.

President Vladimir Putin's case, as NBC News reported it, is that only a full deal will do. He wants Ukrainian forces withdrawn from Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson, the four regions Moscow annexed in September 2022 but never fully captured. He also wants Ukraine to drop its NATO bid, accept strict limits on its military, and end restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church. His stated reason for refusing a general ceasefire is that a pause would let Ukrainian troops rest and replenish weapons. He has warned that Russia will achieve its goals by force if Kyiv refuses those conditions.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's case is the reverse order. He rejects giving up territory Russia has not taken on the battlefield, and he rejects limits on Ukraine's military or on its arrangements with Western partners, which Kyiv calls essential guarantees against another invasion. Ukraine's stated reason for an immediate ceasefire is that it is the necessary first step toward any wider settlement, and that territorial questions can be settled only in a direct meeting between Putin and Zelenskyy.

The talks are already underway, with Vladimir Medinsky leading Russia's delegation and Rustem Umerov leading Ukraine's, and with Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff for the United States. No date for a leaders' meeting is set in today's reporting.

### Progress Watch
Toronto's Dunn House, the housing project named in Canada's 2026 budget as the model for Winnipeg, reported a 52 percent reduction in emergency-room visits and more than 2 million dollars in savings. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12143498/what-winnipeg-can-learn-from-torontos-housing-model/)

# Omni View Top World News
> **At least thirty-four people died off Senegal as a migrant boat headed for the Canary Islands sank.**

**What You Need to Know:** At least 34 people died when a migrant boat sank off Senegal on the way to Spain’s Canary Islands, while arrivals have overwhelmed El Hierro. In Washington, President Trump said deportations might have been too tough and that an arrangement for some undocumented immigrants is doable, with Qatar’s prime minister due at the White House today. This edition also draws on the Omni View Omni View North America desk.

### The Ten
**At least 34 dead after Europe-bound migrant boat sinks off Senegal: BBC World**
Senegal’s interior ministry said at least 34 people died after a small wooden boat capsized between Dakar and Saint-Louis while heading toward Spain’s Canary Islands, the Senegalese Press Agency reported, citing an official source. The ministry said one person was rescued. Saliou Diouf, founder of the Senegalese migrant aid group Boza Fii, told AFP that all the bodies recovered so far were Senegalese, with search operations continuing. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye expressed condolences, urged nationals not to risk the crossings, and pledged on X to keep fighting the networks that organize the journeys and to give young people reasons to hope at home. Spanish group Walking Borders recorded 635 deaths on the Atlantic route to the Canary Islands between January and May 2026, the highest toll among the routes it monitors, and estimated about 21 deaths for every 100 people who reached the islands in that period. Senegalese authorities said they intercepted another boat on Friday carrying 142 migrants, including 23 women, two babies and two other children, nationals of Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea and Nigeria. On El Hierro, local authorities said more than 3,300 people had reached the island in about 30 boats since the beginning of November, almost a third of the population, and a state of emergency was declared on Saturday. Fernando Clavijo, president of the Canary Islands regional government, called the situation absolutely unsustainable, Reuters reported. Nearly one in four young people in Senegal was unemployed in the second quarter of 2026, the country’s statistics agency said, and the interior ministry said on Sunday it would keep combating smuggling networks, including with neighboring countries.
Ranks: people on the Atlantic route and residents of El Hierro · at least 34 dead and arrivals near a third of one island’s population · already, with the search continuing Source: [bbc.co.uk](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cv2d6dpge65go?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)

**Deportation policy ‘might have been too tough’, says Trump, as Miller starts chief-of-staff role: The Guardian**
In the United States, President Donald Trump said he thinks his administration was too aggressive on deportations and that he was open to an arrangement to let some undocumented immigrants remain. He said, “I think it might be too tough, yeah,” adding that a lot of people would say it is great and a lot of people think it is too tough. He said, “We would work something out,” and called such an arrangement “actually doable.” On whether he would endorse a Republican successor for 2028, he said “probably, not necessarily,” and said, “We have a tremendous bench.” He said on Sunday that he “was only kidding” when he announced a day earlier that he had offered the White House press secretary job to Dana White, chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship. The White House schedule shows he meets Qatar’s prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, also foreign minister, in a closed-door meeting today, as the conflict with Iran continues and diplomacy faces obstacles; a U.S. official said Vice President JD Vance is also scheduled to meet the Qatari leader. Attorney Ali Rahnama of the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund said a deportation flight of Iranian nationals bound for Iran by way of Pakistan was canceled Sunday morning without explanation after at least eight Iranians were loaded onto a plane in Mesa, Arizona, headed for Georgia and then Pakistan. The comments come as Stephen Miller starts as White House chief of staff.
Ranks: undocumented immigrants in the United States, and the governments meeting today · a possible change he called doable, plus a canceled flight · the Qatar meeting is today; any new arrangement is not yet a rule Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/09/donald-trump-stephen-miller-immigration-midterms-iran-qatar-economy-latest-news-updates)

**French police officers face trial over beating of black man they accused of not wearing Covid face mask: The Guardian**
In France, three police officers go on trial Monday over the beating of music producer Michel Zecler, now 47, outside his Paris studio on 21 November 2020, when they accused him of failing to wear a mandatory face mask and suspected him of cannabis use. Officers Aurelien B., now 29, Pierre P., 37, and Philippe T. face charges of intentional violence committed in a group and of forgery in an official report, and they face up to 15 years in jail. Their lawyers declined to comment before the trial. The investigation found he suffered about 30 punches and truncheon blows over about five minutes; the medical report noted craniofacial trauma, a wound to the lip and scalp, and a complete rupture of a biceps tendon, leaving him unable to do his job for 45 days. Zecler told AFP he expects the trial to hold the officers accountable, that he was insulted and will say so at the hearing, and that without the studio cameras their report could have sent him to prison. Campaigners and researchers describe police violence as systemic; authorities and law enforcement unions say it is limited to isolated cases. A report last year by the rights ombudswoman, after a survey of more than 5,000 people, said young men perceived as Arab, black or from North Africa are four times more likely to be stopped than the rest of the population and 12 times more likely to face more severe measures, including being frisked. In recent student-led protests a 14-year-old lost most of his teeth when an officer appeared to fire a grenade at close range; in 2024 a judge gave suspended jail sentences over irreversible rectal injuries to Théo Luhaka in a 2017 stop-and-search, and another officer is to be tried over the June 2023 point-blank shooting of 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk.
Ranks: Michel Zecler, three accused officers, and people stopped by French police · a rare criminal trial, not a verdict · the trial starts today Source: [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/09/french-police-officers-face-trial-over-beating-of-black-man-not-wearing-mask-during-covid) · [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-paris-police-officers-go-on-trial-over-2020-beating-of-black-man)

**They signed up for a ‘forever’ cruise. Their dream ran aground after 750 days: The Globe and Mail**
Florida-based Villa Vie Residences said it could no longer operate the Odyssey, and about 200 passengers left the ship at Cambodia’s port of Sihanoukville on October 28, about 750 days into a voyage billed as lasting 1,301 days. Last Wednesday the ship sailed for Singapore without them and is expected to be auctioned to pay the company’s debts as Villa Vie faces potential bankruptcy. The company said it continues to evaluate paths forward, but no financing or transaction has been finalized. Founder Mikael Petterson told Business Insider the project would have been fine, and would have been seen through, if there was no Iran war. Passengers who spoke with The Globe and Mail pointed to company decisions they said left the business vulnerable before the closing of the Strait of Hormuz and the later spike in oil prices. Mary Ann Demsar, of Stony Creek, Ontario, said money was not spent properly and that the strain became clear when residents, not only founders, were asked for money; she said a middle-of-the-night message from owner Kathy Villalba told everybody to be out by 2 p.m. Alberta entrepreneur Gian Perroni said he had sold his house to join, having never taken a cruise, and that cash calls grew more frequent and more outrageous. Demsar credited the crew and Cambodia’s government, which helped with accommodations and food.
Ranks: about 200 passengers who had made the ship home · the voyage has stopped and the ship is headed toward auction · already; bankruptcy is not finalized Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-cambodia-odyssey-forever-cruise-canadians-money-demands/)

**The American and Ukrainian Chaplains Traveling to the War’s Frontlines: Christianity Today**
Ukrainian American Mikhail Pavenko, 34, of Seattle, a power-line repairman, left his wife and two sons on October 29 for his 10th two-week rotation as a military chaplain since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. He said he had never felt that kind of fear, and that on arrival he goes to the front, ministering to soldiers, helping with evacuations, tending the wounded and delivering supplies. He said first-person-view attack drones generate the most fear; some can reach roughly 90 miles per hour and carry warheads powerful enough to disable a tank. In April 2025 in the Zaporizhzhia region, he said, a drone circled the pickup he shared with two other chaplains; he believes a jammer suppressed the operator’s signal, and the drone hit the ground about 15 feet in front of a military truck. Christianity Today reported that Ukraine has more than 400 military chaplains for an estimated 800,000 troops, plus about 700 volunteer chaplains and foreign volunteers, and is about 40 percent short of the number needed, while some soldiers’ morale is low nearly five years into the full-scale war. Pavenko said many fear allies may abandon Ukraine as Russia increases attacks on energy and water systems ahead of winter. The magazine said President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed dismay over a Trump administration deal with President Vladimir Putin to export diesel fuel to the United States, which some critics described as an attempt to sway voters before the November midterms. It cited the Council on Foreign Relations listing a call for Zelensky’s removal, claims that Putin has done more to pursue peace than Zelensky, and disruptions to Starlink service used to intercept drones, and reported that Russia lost more territory than it gained in September and October while attacks on civilians continued.
Ranks: Ukrainian troops and the chaplains who serve them · a reported 40 percent shortfall while drone and winter strikes continue · ongoing Source: [christianitytoday.com](https://www.christianitytoday.com/2026/11/ukraine-war-chaplain-america-frontlines/)

**Ukraine Peace Talks Resume This Week in Abu Dhabi: The New York Times**
U.S.-led talks to end the war between Russia and Ukraine resume this week in Abu Dhabi, and a cease-fire will not be on the table.
Ranks: people living through the Russia-Ukraine war · talks return without a cease-fire on the agenda · this week Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/09/world/europe/ukraine-russia-peace-talks.html)

**Gaza authorities slam global ‘inaction’ after mudslide kills five people: Al Jazeera**
In Gaza, four children and a woman were killed when heavy rain collapsed a sandbank onto their tent, and authorities condemned global inaction.
Ranks: the family in that tent, and people still in Gaza’s camps · five killed, four of them children · already Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/9/gaza-authorities-slam-global-inaction-after-mudslide-kills-five-people?traffic_source=rss)

**Nvidia probe 'to impact the whole of the world': France 24**
Nvidia opened a probe into Jensen Huang after he acknowledged an affair with a woman U.S. officials say worked for Chinese intelligence.
Ranks: Nvidia, its customers, and U.S.-China technology ties · a board probe of the chief executive is underway · now Source: [france24.com](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261109-nvidia-probe-to-impact-the-whole-of-the-world)

**How a Bank Implosion in Paraguay Ensnared a President: The New York Times**
Prosecutors accused Paraguay’s President Santiago Peña of funneling nearly a billion dollars of government funds to the Ueno bank.
Ranks: Paraguay’s public funds and its presidency · a prosecutorial accusation, not a conviction · the charge is public; no trial date is in the report Source: [nytimes.com](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/09/world/americas/paraguay-bank-president-ueno.html)

### Both Sides: Is French police violence systemic or isolated?
What is in dispute is how France should account for police violence, as three officers face a criminal trial over the 21 November 2020 beating of music producer Michel Zecler. No new statute is being voted today. The trial itself is the next formal step, and it opens Monday. The officers are accused. They have not been convicted.

Campaigners and rights groups say the violence is systemic, and that ethnic minorities receive harsher treatment than white people. Their strongest reason is the pattern they cite around this case and beyond it. France’s human rights ombudswoman said police used racist insults, according to four witnesses. Zecler says he was insulted with a racist slur and will repeat that at the hearing. A report last year by the ombudswoman, after a survey of more than 5,000 people, said young men perceived as Arab, black or from North Africa are four times more likely to be stopped than the rest of the population and 12 times more likely to face more severe measures, including frisks. Campaigners also point to other filmed cases, including the June 2023 shooting of 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk and the 2017 injuries to Théo Luhaka, for which a judge in 2024 gave three officers suspended jail sentences.

Authorities and law enforcement unions say brutality is limited to isolated cases. Their strongest reason is that a criminal trial is the exception: most alleged brutality is handled internally, and guilty verdicts are rare. Their lawyers declined to comment before the trial. If a court convicts them, the charges carry up to 15 years in jail. No article gives a verdict date.
